# NBP Test Preparation — National Bank of Pakistan Practice Guide | BankTest.pk

Source: https://banktesthelp.github.io/nbp.html
# NBP Test Preparation — National Bank of Pakistan 
By BankTest.pk Team · Last updated: 26 November 2026 
A complete practice guide for National Bank of Pakistan recruitment tests: typical test pattern, section-wise syllabus, common posts and free original practice quizzes. 
## Overview 
The National Bank of Pakistan (NBP) is Pakistan's largest public-sector commercial bank, with branches across the country and abroad. NBP recruits regularly for officer, management trainee, cashier and customer-service positions. Recruitment is advertised in national newspapers and on the bank's official channels, and the screening test is usually conducted by an external testing service on behalf of the bank. 
NBP tests follow the standard Pakistani bank-test format: multiple-choice questions covering English, mathematics, analytical reasoning, general knowledge, current affairs and banking. Competition is high because public-sector banking jobs are sought after, so strong preparation in every section matters. 
## Common Posts 
### Management Trainee Officer (MTO) 
NBP's flagship entry-level officer program for fresh graduates. MTOs go through structured training and are groomed for branch and head-office roles. The test is usually the toughest NBP screens, with strong emphasis on analytical reasoning and English. 
### Officer Grade-II (OG-II) 
A general officer position involving branch operations, customer handling and credit support. Candidates typically need a bachelor's or master's degree; the test follows the standard multi-section pattern below. 
### Cashier / Teller 
Front-line branch staff handling cash transactions. The test leans toward basic arithmetic, speed and accuracy, plus simple English and general knowledge. 
### Customer Service Representative 
Handles customer queries, account opening and service requests. Expect a balance of English communication, basic math and general awareness in the screening test. 
## Typical Test Pattern 
This is a typical pattern compiled from publicly advertised formats for NBP-style bank tests. Actual sections, question counts and time limits vary by post and by the testing service conducting the test — always verify with the official job advertisement. 
Section Questions Time 
English 20 90 minutes total 
Mathematics 20 
IQ & Analytical Reasoning 10 
General Knowledge & Current Affairs 20 
Banking & Finance 10 
Total 80 90 min 
This is a typical pattern compiled from publicly advertised formats. Actual sections, counts and time vary by post and testing service — always verify with the official job advertisement. 
## Syllabus Breakdown 
### English (20 questions) 
Grammar: tenses, subject-verb agreement, articles, prepositions 
Vocabulary: synonyms, antonyms, one-word substitution, idioms 
Sentence correction and error spotting 
Fill in the blanks with appropriate words 
Reading comprehension passages with inference questions 
### Mathematics (20 questions) 
Percentages, profit and loss, discounts and markups 
Ratio, proportion and partnership problems 
Averages, ages and mixture problems 
Simple and compound interest calculations 
Time, speed and distance; time and work 
Basic algebra and number series 
### IQ & Analytical Reasoning (10 questions) 
Number and letter series completion 
Analogies and classification 
Coding and decoding patterns 
Blood relations and direction sense 
Basic logical deductions and statement-conclusion items 
### General Knowledge & Current Affairs (20 questions) 
Pakistan studies: history, provinces, national symbols 
Geography: rivers, capitals, important landmarks 
Recent national news, government policies and appointments 
International affairs and major world events 
Sports, awards and notable personalities 
### Banking & Finance (10 questions) 
Functions of commercial banks and the State Bank of Pakistan 
Banking terms: deposits, loans, markup, collateral, LC 
Types of accounts and basic financial instruments 
Basic Islamic banking concepts (Mudarabah, Murabaha) 
Inflation, GDP and other elementary economic terms 
## Practice by Topic 
Start with 15-question practice quizzes for each section. All questions are original practice material with explanations. [English](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=nbp&topic=english&count=15)[Mathematics](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=nbp&topic=math&count=15)[IQ & Reasoning](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=nbp&topic=iq&count=15)[General Knowledge](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=nbp&topic=gk&count=15)[Current Affairs](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=nbp&topic=current-affairs&count=15)[Banking & Finance](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=nbp&topic=banking&count=15)
Ready for the full experience? [Take a full-length 50-question full test](https://banktesthelp.github.io/mock.html). 
## NBP Preparation Tips 
Master the basics first: percentages, ratios and averages appear in almost every NBP math section. Drill them until you can solve each question in under a minute. 
Read daily for current affairs: spend 20 minutes each day on national news and economic headlines — current affairs is the highest-weightage section alongside English and math. 
Build English vocabulary actively: learn 10 new words daily with synonyms and antonyms, and practice error-spotting questions regularly. 
Practice reasoning puzzles: series, coding-decoding and blood relations reward pattern recognition — the more puzzles you attempt, the faster you become. 
Learn banking terminology: even non-commerce graduates can score full marks in the banking section by memorizing key terms and SBP functions. 
Take timed full tests: 90 minutes for 80 questions means roughly one minute per question. Simulate the pressure with full-length tests. 
Revise mistakes weekly: keep a notebook of questions you got wrong and review it before every full test. 
Check the official advertisement: eligibility, syllabus hints and test details change with each recruitment — confirm everything against the official NBP advertisement. 
## Also Preparing for Other Banks? 
The test pattern is similar across Pakistani banks. Continue your preparation with our [SBP guide](https://banktesthelp.github.io/sbp.html), the [topic breakdowns](https://banktesthelp.github.io/topics.html), or the detailed [4–6 week study plan](https://banktesthelp.github.io/preparation-guide.html). 
Official links: [National Bank of Pakistan](https://www.nbp.com.pk/)and the [NBP careers page](https://www.nbp.com.pk/careers)— check current openings and verify the test syllabus with the official job advertisement.

# SBP Test Preparation — State Bank of Pakistan Practice Guide | BankTest.pk

Source: https://banktesthelp.github.io/sbp.html
# SBP Test Preparation — State Bank of Pakistan 
By BankTest.pk Team · Last updated: 26 November 2026 
A complete practice guide for State Bank of Pakistan recruitment: typical test pattern, section-wise syllabus, flagship hiring programs and free original practice quizzes. 
## Overview 
The State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) is Pakistan's central bank. It regulates the banking sector, manages monetary policy, issues currency and oversees the country's financial stability. Because of its prestige and role in the economy, SBP jobs attract some of the strongest candidates in the country, and its entry tests are among the most competitive bank exams in Pakistan. 
SBP conducts recruitment for its flagship officer programs and other positions through advertised tests, usually administered by a testing service. The screening test is a multiple-choice paper covering English, quantitative ability, analytical reasoning, general knowledge, current affairs and banking and economy. 
## Flagship Hiring Programs 
### YPIP — Young Professionals Induction Program 
SBP's premier induction scheme for young professionals with master's degrees. Selected candidates receive structured training at the central bank and are placed in key departments. The screening test is highly competitive, with strong weightage on analytical reasoning and quantitative skills. 
### SBOTS — SBP Officers Training Scheme 
A training scheme that inducts officers into the central bank's cadres. Candidates go through a written test, group discussion and interview stages. The written test follows the multi-section pattern below, with particular emphasis on English and current affairs. 
### Other Officer & Specialist Positions 
SBP also advertises positions for economists, IT specialists, legal officers and support staff from time to time. The screening test generally follows the same multi-section format, with the syllabus adjusted to the nature of the post. 
## Typical Test Pattern 
This is a typical pattern compiled from publicly advertised formats for SBP-style central bank tests. Actual sections, question counts and time limits vary by program and by the testing service conducting the test — always verify with the official job advertisement. 
Section Questions Time 
English 20 90 minutes total 
Quantitative 20 
Analytical / Logical Reasoning 15 
General Knowledge & Current Affairs 15 
Banking & Economy 10 
Total 80 90 min 
This is a typical pattern compiled from publicly advertised formats. Actual sections, counts and time vary by post and testing service — always verify with the official job advertisement. 
## Syllabus Breakdown 
### English (20 questions) 
Advanced grammar: tenses, conditionals, reported speech, voice 
Vocabulary in context: synonyms, antonyms, idioms and phrases 
Sentence completion and paragraph-based questions 
Reading comprehension with inference and tone questions 
Precis-style understanding of long passages 
### Quantitative (20 questions) 
Percentages, profit and loss, discounts 
Ratio, proportion and averages 
Simple and compound interest 
Time, speed, distance and work-rate problems 
Basic algebra, equations and number properties 
Data interpretation from tables and charts 
### Analytical / Logical Reasoning (15 questions) 
Number, letter and mixed series 
Analogies and odd-one-out 
Coding-decoding and symbolic logic 
Blood relations and seating arrangements 
Statement–assumption and statement–conclusion items 
### General Knowledge & Current Affairs (15 questions) 
Pakistan's political and constitutional developments 
Recent economic news: budget, inflation, exchange rate 
International organizations and current world events 
Pakistan studies: history, geography, culture 
Awards, sports and notable personalities 
### Banking & Economy (10 questions) 
Role and functions of the State Bank of Pakistan 
Monetary policy tools: policy rate, reserve requirements, open market operations 
Commercial banking operations and instruments 
Inflation, GDP, fiscal vs. monetary policy basics 
Islamic banking modes and their features 
## Practice by Topic 
Start with 15-question practice quizzes for each section. All questions are original practice material with explanations. Ready for the full experience? [Take a full-length 50-question full test](https://banktesthelp.github.io/mock.html). 
## SBP Preparation Tips 
Expect a tougher reasoning section: SBP tests reward analytical depth. Practice complex series, arrangements and logical deductions beyond the basics. 
Follow the economy closely: read SBP's own announcements, the federal budget highlights and inflation reports — central-bank tests love economy questions. 
Know what SBP does: understand monetary policy, the policy rate, and SBP's regulatory role in detail; this section is easy marks for prepared candidates. 
Strengthen data interpretation: tables and charts appear in the quantitative section — practice reading them quickly and accurately. 
Read opinion pieces, not just headlines: SBP-level English comprehension rewards readers who engage with editorials and analytical writing. 
Time yourself strictly: with 80 questions in 90 minutes, practice full-length timed papers so the real test feels familiar. 
Prepare for later stages too: SBP programs often include group discussions and interviews — build general awareness alongside test skills. 
Verify with the official advertisement: programs, eligibility and test formats are announced officially — always confirm details against the SBP advertisement. 
## Also Preparing for Other Banks? 
The skills you build for SBP transfer directly to commercial bank tests. Continue with our [NBP guide](https://banktesthelp.github.io/nbp.html), the [topic breakdowns](https://banktesthelp.github.io/topics.html), or the detailed [4–6 week study plan](https://banktesthelp.github.io/preparation-guide.html). 
Official source: SBOTS recruitment is run by the State Bank of Pakistan itself — test details appear in the official SBP advertisement. The written test is often administered by an external testing service such as [NTS](https://www.nts.org.pk/). Always verify the syllabus and test date with the official advertisement.

# HBL Test Preparation — Practice Guide | BankTest.pk

Source: https://banktesthelp.github.io/hbl.html
# HBL Test Preparation 
By BankTest.pk Team · Last updated: 26 November 2026 
Free practice material for HBL (Habib Bank Limited) recruitment tests — typical test pattern and topic quizzes to help you prepare. 
HBL (Habib Bank Limited) is one of Pakistan's largest commercial banks, with a nationwide branch network and a long history in the country's banking sector. The bank regularly hires management trainees, officers and support staff through written screening tests, often conducted by external testing services. 
HBL tests are typically aptitude-based: they check English comprehension, basic quantitative skills, logical reasoning and general awareness. A strong command of these four areas is enough for most screening stages. 
## Typical Test Pattern 
Section Typical Questions What to Expect 
English 20 Vocabulary, grammar, sentence completion, reading comprehension 
Quantitative 25 Percentages, ratios, averages, profit & loss, basic algebra 
Analytical & IQ 20 Number series, odd one out, analogies, logical puzzles 
General Knowledge & Current Affairs 25 Pakistan studies, banking basics, recent economic news 
Test patterns vary by post and testing service. Always verify the syllabus with the official HBL job advertisement. 
## How to Prepare for the HBL Test 
HBL screening tests are aptitude-based, so the best preparation is regular timed practice in the four core sections — English, quantitative ability, analytical reasoning and general knowledge. Start by taking one quiz from each section on this page to find your weakest area, then give that section half of your daily study time until it catches up. The pattern table above shows what each section covers; use it as a checklist and tick off every topic as you practise it. 
For English, revise grammar rules (tenses, prepositions, subject-verb agreement) and learn vocabulary through sentence completion rather than word lists — the test checks whether you can use a word correctly, not whether you can recite its dictionary meaning. For math, practise percentages, ratios, averages and profit-and-loss problems without a calculator, because speed matters as much as accuracy. For reasoning, work on number series, odd-one-out and analogy questions every day; they follow a small set of patterns, and once you recognise them your score jumps quickly. For general knowledge, revise Pakistan studies and keep up with current affairs from the last three months, especially banking and economic news. 
## Two-Week Study Plan 
Week 1 — foundations: one topic quiz per day, reading every explanation afterwards. Write down every formula and fact you miss in a small notebook and revise it each evening. Spend extra time on the section where your score is lowest. 
Week 2 — timed practice: take the full-length mock test twice under real conditions — no phone, no breaks, strict time limit. After each mock, spend an hour on your weakest section only. In the last two days, revise your notebook and retake your lowest-scoring quizzes. Do not start any new topic the night before the test. 
## Frequently Asked Questions 
How many questions are in the HBL test? The pattern varies by post and testing service, but the typical screening test follows the four-section format in the table above — roughly 90 questions across English, quantitative, analytical and general knowledge sections. 
What is the passing score? Most bank recruitment tests in Pakistan set the passing mark around 60%. Aim to score at least 60% consistently in our practice quizzes before the real test. 
Is there negative marking? The marking scheme is stated in the job advertisement and the instructions on your question paper. Most bank screening tests do not deduct marks for wrong answers, but always read the instructions carefully before you start. 
Where do I find official HBL job advertisements? Check the [HBL website](https://www.hbl.com/)for current openings and the exact eligibility criteria of each post. HBL tests are often conducted by external testing services such as [NTS](https://www.nts.org.pk/)— always verify the test syllabus with the official job advertisement.

# MCB Test Preparation — Practice Guide | BankTest.pk

Source: https://banktesthelp.github.io/mcb.html
# MCB Test Preparation 
By BankTest.pk Team · Last updated: 26 November 2026 
Free practice material for MCB Bank Limited recruitment tests — typical test pattern and topic quizzes to help you prepare. 
MCB Bank Limited (formerly Muslim Commercial Bank) is one of Pakistan's largest private-sector banks, known for its strong corporate banking franchise and wide retail network. The bank recruits management trainees, officers and branch staff through aptitude-based written tests, usually administered by an external testing service. 
MCB screening tests generally follow the standard banking aptitude format: English language skills, quantitative ability, analytical reasoning and general knowledge with a banking flavour. Practising these sections regularly is the most reliable way to clear the cutoff. 
## Typical Test Pattern 
Section Typical Questions What to Expect 
English 20 Grammar, vocabulary, sentence correction, short passages 
Quantitative 25 Arithmetic, percentages, ratios, time & work, simple algebra 
Analytical & IQ 20 Series completion, coding-decoding, blood relations, directions 
General Knowledge & Current Affairs 25 Pakistan affairs, economy, banking terms, recent developments 
Test patterns vary by post and testing service. Always verify the syllabus with the official MCB job advertisement. 
## How to Prepare for the MCB Test 
MCB screening tests follow the standard banking aptitude format, so the most effective preparation is section-wise timed practice. Begin with a diagnostic run: take one quiz from each section on this page and note your scores. The section with the lowest score gets half of your daily study time until it improves. The pattern table above is your syllabus — work through it topic by topic rather than jumping randomly between quizzes. 
For English, focus on vocabulary in context, sentence correction and short comprehension passages; reading one English newspaper editorial a day builds vocabulary and current-affairs knowledge together. For math, drill percentages, ratios, averages and profit-and-loss problems until you can solve them mentally — calculators are not part of the test, so speed comes from familiarity. For reasoning, practise number series, analogies and coding-decoding daily; these questions follow a small set of patterns, and recognising them quickly is worth many marks. For general knowledge, revise Pakistan studies basics and follow the last three months of economic news, especially anything involving the State Bank, inflation, exchange rates and the banking sector. 
## Two-Week Study Plan 
Week 1 — foundations: one topic quiz per day, reading every explanation afterwards — including the explanations for questions you got right. Keep a notebook of formulas and facts you keep forgetting, and revise it every evening. 
Week 2 — timed practice: take the full-length mock test twice under real test conditions — no phone, no breaks, strict time limit. After each mock, spend an hour on your weakest section only. In the final two days, revise your notebook and retake the quizzes you scored lowest on; do not start any new topic the night before the test. 
## Frequently Asked Questions 
How many questions are in the MCB test? The pattern varies by post and testing service, but the typical screening test follows the four-section format in the table above — roughly 90 questions across English, quantitative, analytical and general knowledge sections. 
What is the passing score? Most bank recruitment tests in Pakistan set the passing mark around 60%. Aim to score at least 60% consistently in our practice quizzes before the real test. 
Is there negative marking? The marking scheme is stated in the job advertisement and the instructions on your question paper. Most bank screening tests do not deduct marks for wrong answers, but always read the instructions carefully before you start. 
Where do I apply for MCB jobs? Check the official MCB Bank careers page for current openings and the exact eligibility criteria of each post: [MCB Bank careers](https://www.mcb.com.pk/careers)and the [MCB Bank website](https://www.mcb.com.pk/). Always verify the test syllabus with the official job advertisement.

Free practice material for UBL (United Bank Limited) recruitment tests — typical test pattern and topic quizzes to help you prepare. 
UBL (United Bank Limited) is a leading commercial bank in Pakistan with a large domestic and international presence. It hires management trainees, relationship officers and branch staff through competitive written tests, often conducted by independent testing services.

## HR / Personality Interview Prep 
Recent UBL OG-IV and BSO screening rounds also include personality-style statements. These have no right or wrong answers — they assess traits like empathy, calmness, teamwork and reliability. Read each statement and decide how honestly it describes you: 
I understand and care about other people's feelings. 
I don't talk much. 
I usually stay calm and relaxed. 
I find it hard to understand deep or difficult ideas. 
I have a good imagination. 
I don't like to think about difficult or deep ideas. 
My mood changes a lot. 
I often forget to keep things in their proper place. 
I enjoy being the center of attention at a party. 
I avoid doing my duties. 
I like to keep things in order. 
I finish my work quickly. 
I don't care about other people's problems. 
I prefer to stay in the background. 
I can feel what others are feeling. 
I like talking to many people at parties. 
I have many new ideas. 
I rarely feel sad. 
I make people feel comfortable. 
Tip: answer steadily and honestly — recruiters look for consistency across similar statements (for example, the statements about calmness, about ideas, and about caring for others). 
Official source: check the UBL website for current openings and the exact eligibility criteria of each post. UBL tests are often conducted by external testing services such as [NTS](https://www.nts.org.pk/)— always verify the test syllabus with the official job advertisement.

# Meezan Bank Test Preparation — Practice Guide | BankTest.pk

Source: https://banktesthelp.github.io/meezan.html
# Meezan Bank Test Preparation 
By BankTest.pk Team · Last updated: 26 November 2026 
Free practice material for Meezan Bank recruitment tests — typical test pattern and topic quizzes to help you prepare. 
Meezan Bank is Pakistan's first and largest Islamic commercial bank, operating a fully Shariah-compliant banking model. It recruits management trainees, officers and branch staff through competitive written tests, usually run by external testing services. 
Alongside the standard English, quantitative and reasoning sections, Meezan tests often include questions on Islamic banking concepts — so it pays to know basic terms like Murabaha, Ijarah and Mudarabah before test day. 
## Typical Test Pattern 
Section Typical Questions What to Expect 
English 20 Grammar, vocabulary, sentence completion, comprehension 
Quantitative 25 Arithmetic, percentages, profit & loss, basic algebra 
Analytical & IQ 20 Series, analogies, logical reasoning, odd one out 
General Knowledge & Current Affairs 25 Pakistan affairs, economy, Islamic banking terms, current events 
Test patterns vary by post and testing service. Always verify the syllabus with the official Meezan Bank job advertisement. 
## How to Prepare for the Meezan Bank Test 
Meezan Bank tests follow the standard banking aptitude format with one important difference: as Pakistan's first Islamic bank, Meezan includes Islamic banking questions alongside English, math, IQ and general knowledge. Give the Islamic banking section real study time — candidates who prepare only the aptitude sections lose easy marks here. Learn the basic modes of Islamic finance first: Mudarabah (profit-sharing), Musharakah (partnership), Ijarah (leasing) and Murabaha (cost-plus sale), and understand what Riba is and why Islamic banks avoid it. Our banking quiz on this page includes Islamic banking questions to get you started. 
For English, revise grammar, vocabulary in context and short comprehension passages. For math, drill percentages, ratios, averages and profit-and-loss problems without a calculator. For reasoning, practise number series, analogies and coding-decoding daily — these follow a small set of patterns that become easy once you recognise them. For general knowledge, revise Pakistan studies and follow the last three months of economic news, especially news about Islamic banking, the State Bank and the economy. 
## Two-Week Study Plan 
Week 1 — foundations: one topic quiz per day, reading every explanation afterwards. Spend one full day on Islamic banking concepts alone — write down each mode of finance with a one-line example (for example, Ijarah is like renting an asset instead of lending money for it). Keep a notebook of formulas and facts you keep forgetting, and revise it every evening. 
Week 2 — timed practice: take the full-length mock test twice under real test conditions — no phone, no breaks, strict time limit. After each mock, spend an hour on your weakest section only. In the final two days, revise your notebook and retake the quizzes you scored lowest on; do not start any new topic the night before the test. 
## Frequently Asked Questions 
How many questions are in the Meezan Bank test? The pattern varies by post and testing service, but the typical screening test follows the four-section format in the table above, plus Islamic banking questions — roughly 90 questions across English, quantitative, analytical, general knowledge and Islamic banking sections. 
What is the passing score? Most bank recruitment tests in Pakistan set the passing mark around 60%. Aim to score at least 60% consistently in our practice quizzes before the real test. 
Is there negative marking? The marking scheme is stated in the job advertisement and the instructions on your question paper. Most bank screening tests do not deduct marks for wrong answers, but always read the instructions carefully before you start. 
Where do I find official Meezan Bank job advertisements? Check the Meezan Bank website and its careers section for current openings, and verify the test syllabus with the official job advertisement. Meezan Bank tests are often conducted by external testing services such as [NTS](https://www.nts.org.pk/).

# Allied Bank Test Preparation 
By BankTest.pk Team · Last updated: 26 November 2026 
Free practice material for Allied Bank Limited recruitment tests — typical test pattern and topic quizzes to help you prepare. 
Allied Bank Limited (ABL) is one of Pakistan's largest private-sector banks, with an extensive branch network across the country. The bank recruits management trainees, officers and frontline staff through written aptitude tests, typically administered by external testing services. 
Allied Bank screening tests usually follow the standard banking aptitude format — English, quantitative ability, analytical reasoning and general knowledge. Consistent timed practice in each section is the best preparation. 
## Typical Test Pattern 
Section Typical Questions What to Expect 
English 20 Vocabulary, grammar, sentence correction, comprehension 
Quantitative 25 Percentages, ratios, averages, profit & loss, algebra basics 
Analytical & IQ 20 Number series, analogies, coding-decoding, logical puzzles 
General Knowledge & Current Affairs 25 Pakistan studies, economy, banking terms, current events 
Test patterns vary by post and testing service. Always verify the syllabus with the official Allied Bank job advertisement. 
## How to Prepare for the Allied Bank Test 
The Allied Bank screening test rewards steady, section-wise practice rather than last-minute cramming. Start with the two sections that carry the most weight — quantitative ability and general knowledge — and build English and reasoning around them. Work through the pattern table above one section at a time, and take every quiz on this page at least twice: once untimed, to learn the question types, and once against the clock, to build speed. 
For English, focus on vocabulary in context, sentence correction and short comprehension passages; reading one English newspaper editorial a day covers vocabulary and current affairs at the same time. For math, master percentages, ratios, averages and profit-and-loss shortcuts — these four topics appear in almost every banking test. For analytical reasoning, practise number series, analogies and coding-decoding daily; these are pattern-recognition skills that improve quickly with repetition. For general knowledge, revise Pakistan studies basics (provinces, rivers, dams, constitutional history) and follow the last three months of economic news, especially anything about the State Bank, inflation and the banking sector. 
## Two-Week Study Plan 
Week 1 — foundations: take one topic quiz per day (English, math, IQ, GK, current affairs, banking) and read every explanation, even for questions you answered correctly. Keep a notebook of the formulas and facts you keep forgetting, and revise it each evening. 
Week 2 — timed practice: take the full-length mock test twice, under real test conditions — no phone, no breaks, and a strict time limit. After each mock, spend an hour on your weakest section only. In the final two days, revise your notebook and retake the quizzes you scored lowest on; do not start any new topic the night before the test. 
## Frequently Asked Questions 
How many questions are in the Allied Bank test? The pattern varies by post and testing service, but the typical screening test follows the four-section format in the table above — roughly 90 questions across English, quantitative, analytical and general knowledge sections. 
What is the passing score? Most bank recruitment tests in Pakistan set the passing mark around 60%. Aim to score at least 60% consistently in our practice quizzes before the real test. 
Is there negative marking? The marking scheme is stated in the job advertisement and the instructions on your question paper. Most bank screening tests do not deduct marks for wrong answers, but always read the instructions carefully before you start. 
Where do I apply for Allied Bank jobs? Check the official Allied Bank careers page for current openings and the exact eligibility criteria of each post: [Allied Bank careers](https://www.abl.com/careers)and the [Allied Bank website](https://www.abl.com/). Always verify the test syllabus with the official job advertisement.

# Bank of Punjab Test Preparation — Practice Guide | BankTest.pk

Source: https://banktesthelp.github.io/bop.html
# Bank of Punjab Test Preparation 
By BankTest.pk Team · Last updated: 26 November 2026 
Free practice material for Bank of Punjab (BOP) recruitment tests — typical test pattern and topic quizzes to help you prepare. 
The Bank of Punjab (BOP) is a provincial government bank headquartered in Lahore, serving customers across Pakistan with a strong presence in Punjab. It hires officers, management trainees and branch staff through written screening tests, often conducted by external testing services such as NTS, PTS or OTS. 
BOP screening tests generally follow the standard banking aptitude format: English, quantitative ability, analytical reasoning and general knowledge with current affairs. Candidates from all provinces can apply for most advertised posts. 🔥 BOP Online Assessment Mock Test — 60 MCQs · 75 minutes: practice the exact format of the current online assessment (CSO / PBO, Branch Banking Sales) with original questions and a section-wise score breakdown. [Start the BOP mock test →](https://banktesthelp.github.io/mock.html?bank=bop)
## Current Online Assessment (2026) 
For the ongoing CSO / PBO (Branch Banking Sales) hiring, shortlisted candidates receive an online assessment by email. It is a 60-MCQ online test of about 1 hour 15 minutes , taken from home — camera off, and it works on a mobile phone too. Use a stable internet connection and a fully charged device, take the test in a quiet place, and do not close or refresh the browser during the test: some candidates who were logged out mid-test reported seeing "Test already attempted" on re-login. If that happens, contact BOP's recruitment team through the email that sent your test invitation instead of retrying repeatedly. 
## Typical Test Pattern — Online Assessment (60 MCQs, ~75 Minutes) 
Section Questions What to Expect 
English 12 Sentence completion, synonyms & antonyms, grammar, comprehension 
Quantitative / Math 12 Percentages, averages, profit & loss, ratios, simple interest, time & work 
Analytical & IQ 12 Number & letter series, analogies, coding, odd one out, logical reasoning 
General Knowledge 10 Pakistan studies, Punjab affairs, geography, science, everyday facts 
Current Affairs 6 Pakistan economy, SBP, digital banking (Roshan Digital Account, NIFT), IMF programme 
Banking & Finance 8 Account types, KYC, cheques & pay orders, Islamic banking, SBP functions 
This pattern is modelled on the NTS Bank of Punjab sample paper (English, analytical reasoning, quantitative, general knowledge and banking sections) and the current 60-MCQ online assessment reported by candidates. Test patterns vary by post and testing service. Always verify the syllabus with the official Bank of Punjab job advertisement. 
## How to Prepare for the BOP Online Assessment 
The current BOP online assessment is a 60-question test in about 75 minutes — roughly 75 seconds per question. That makes time management the skill that matters most. Practise with a timer from day one: our BOP mock test above uses the same 60-question, 75-minute format, so take it at least twice before your test day. If a question takes more than a minute, mark it mentally, move on, and come back only if time remains — one hard question is never worth three easy ones. 
Section by section: English is mostly sentence completion, synonyms and antonyms, grammar and a short comprehension passage — revise vocabulary in context rather than word lists. Math is percentages, averages, profit and loss, ratios, simple interest and time-and-work; drill these without a calculator. Analytical and IQ questions are number and letter series, analogies, coding and odd-one-out — they follow a small set of patterns, so daily practice pays off fast. General knowledge covers Pakistan studies, Punjab affairs, geography and science, while current affairs leans on the economy, SBP and digital banking topics such as the Roshan Digital Account and NIFT. Banking questions test basics: account types, KYC, cheques and pay orders, and SBP's functions. 
## Two-Week Study Plan 
Week 1 — foundations: one topic quiz per day from the list below, reading every explanation afterwards. Keep a notebook of formulas and facts you keep forgetting, and revise it every evening. 
Week 2 — timed practice: take the 60-MCQ BOP mock test twice under real conditions — quiet room, charged device, stable internet, no breaks. After each mock, spend an hour on your weakest section only. In the final two days, revise your notebook and retake your lowest-scoring quizzes. On test day, log in early, keep your device charged, and do not close or refresh the browser during the test. 
## Frequently Asked Questions 
Can I take the BOP online assessment on a mobile phone? Yes. Candidates have completed the test on mobile phones, but a laptop or desktop with a stable connection is safer — a bigger screen makes reading passages easier and reduces accidental taps. 
Is the camera on during the test? Candidates report the camera was off for the current online assessment. Follow the instructions in your test invitation email, because the format can change between hiring rounds. 
What if I am logged out during the test? Do not keep retrying — candidates who were logged out mid-test reported seeing "Test already attempted" on re-login. Contact BOP's recruitment team through the email that sent your test invitation. 
Where do I apply for Bank of Punjab jobs? Check the official Bank of Punjab careers page for current openings and the exact eligibility criteria of each post: [Bank of Punjab careers](https://www.bop.com.pk/careers)and the [Bank of Punjab website](https://www.bop.com.pk/). BOP tests are often conducted by external testing services such as [NTS](https://www.nts.org.pk/)— always verify the syllabus with the official job advertisement.

# Test Topics — Bank Exam Syllabus Breakdown | BankTest.pk

Source: https://banktesthelp.github.io/topics.html
# Test Topics — Bank Exam Syllabus Breakdown 
Pakistani bank recruitment tests draw from six core areas. This page breaks down what each section checks, lists the key sub-topics, and links you straight into practice quizzes. 
## English 
The English section tests grammar, vocabulary and comprehension. Bank tests typically include error-spotting, sentence correction, synonyms and antonyms, and at least one reading passage. Since bank jobs involve written communication, this section carries significant weight in most screening tests. 
Tenses and subject-verb agreement 
Prepositions, articles and conjunctions 
Synonyms, antonyms and one-word substitution 
Idioms, phrases and phrasal verbs 
Sentence correction and error spotting 
Reading comprehension and inference 
Read the full strategy: [English Preparation Guide for Bank Tests](https://banktesthelp.github.io/english-preparation-guide.html)[NBP English quiz](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=nbp&topic=english&count=15)[SBP English quiz](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=sbp&topic=english&count=15)
More banks: [HBL](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=hbl&topic=english&count=15)· [MCB](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=mcb&topic=english&count=15)· [UBL](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=ubl&topic=english&count=15)· [Meezan](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=meezan&topic=english&count=15)· [Allied](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=allied&topic=english&count=15)· [BOP](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=bop&topic=english&count=15)
## Mathematics 
The math section checks numerical ability and problem-solving speed. Questions are usually at the matric-to-intermediate level, focusing on arithmetic and basic algebra rather than advanced mathematics. Calculators are not allowed, so mental math and shortcut methods give a real advantage here. 
Percentages, profit and loss, discounts 
Ratio, proportion and averages 
Simple and compound interest 
Time, speed and distance; time and work 
Basic algebra and number series 
Data interpretation from tables and charts 
Read the full strategy: [Quantitative & Math Preparation Guide for Bank Tests](https://banktesthelp.github.io/math-preparation-guide.html)[NBP Math quiz](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=nbp&topic=math&count=15)[SBP Math quiz](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=sbp&topic=math&count=15)
More banks: [HBL](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=hbl&topic=math&count=15)· [MCB](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=mcb&topic=math&count=15)· [UBL](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=ubl&topic=math&count=15)· [Meezan](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=meezan&topic=math&count=15)· [Allied](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=allied&topic=math&count=15)· [BOP](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=bop&topic=math&count=15)
## IQ & Reasoning 
This section measures logical thinking and pattern recognition rather than memorized knowledge. Questions include series completion, analogies, coding-decoding and puzzles like blood relations. Practice is the key — the more patterns you have seen, the faster you will recognize them in the test. 
Number and letter series 
Analogies and classification 
Coding and decoding 
Blood relations and direction sense 
Seating arrangements and puzzles 
Statement, assumption and conclusion logic [NBP IQ quiz](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=nbp&topic=iq&count=15)[SBP IQ quiz](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=sbp&topic=iq&count=15)
More banks: [HBL](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=hbl&topic=iq&count=15)· [MCB](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=mcb&topic=iq&count=15)· [UBL](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=ubl&topic=iq&count=15)· [Meezan](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=meezan&topic=iq&count=15)· [Allied](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=allied&topic=iq&count=15)· [BOP](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=bop&topic=iq&count=15)
## General Knowledge 
General knowledge covers Pakistan studies, geography, science basics and everyday facts. Unlike other sections, it cannot be reasoned out — you either know the answer or you don't. A steady habit of reading and revising facts, plus regular quizzes, is the most reliable way to build this section. 
Pakistan history and the independence movement 
Provinces, capitals, rivers and landmarks 
National symbols, days and personalities 
Basic science: inventions, units, human body 
World geography and international organizations [NBP GK quiz](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=nbp&topic=gk&count=15)[SBP GK quiz](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=sbp&topic=gk&count=15)
More banks: [HBL](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=hbl&topic=gk&count=15)· [MCB](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=mcb&topic=gk&count=15)· [UBL](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=ubl&topic=gk&count=15)· [Meezan](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=meezan&topic=gk&count=15)· [Allied](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=allied&topic=gk&count=15)· [BOP](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=bop&topic=gk&count=15)
## Current Affairs 
Current affairs tests your awareness of recent national and international events. Bank tests favor economic and financial news — budgets, policy rates, exchange rates and banking-sector developments — alongside major political events and sports. Focus your reading on the last 6–12 months before the test. 
National politics and government policies 
Economic news: budget, inflation, exchange rate 
Banking-sector and SBP announcements 
International events and summits 
Sports, awards and notable appointments [NBP Current Affairs quiz](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=nbp&topic=current-affairs&count=15)[SBP Current Affairs quiz](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=sbp&topic=current-affairs&count=15)
More banks: [HBL](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=hbl&topic=current-affairs&count=15)· [MCB](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=mcb&topic=current-affairs&count=15)· [UBL](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=ubl&topic=current-affairs&count=15)· [Meezan](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=meezan&topic=current-affairs&count=15)· [Allied](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=allied&topic=current-affairs&count=15)· [BOP](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=bop&topic=current-affairs&count=15)
## Banking & Finance 
This is the most bank-specific section and a scoring opportunity for everyone, including non-commerce graduates. Questions cover banking terminology, the role of the State Bank of Pakistan, basic economics and Islamic banking concepts. The syllabus is narrow enough to master with focused study. 
Functions of commercial banks and SBP 
Banking terms: deposits, markup, collateral, LC 
Types of accounts and financial instruments 
Inflation, GDP, fiscal and monetary policy 
Islamic banking: Mudarabah, Murabaha, Ijarah 
Monetary policy tools and the policy rate 
Bank-specific guides: [Meezan Bank PBO Test Preparation Guide](https://banktesthelp.github.io/meezan-pbo-guide.html)· [SBOTS 29th Batch Complete Preparation Guide](https://banktesthelp.github.io/sbots-guide.html)[NBP Banking quiz](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=nbp&topic=banking&count=15)[SBP Banking quiz](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=sbp&topic=banking&count=15)
More banks: [HBL](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=hbl&topic=banking&count=15)· [MCB](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=mcb&topic=banking&count=15)· [UBL](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=ubl&topic=banking&count=15)· [Meezan](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=meezan&topic=banking&count=15)· [Allied](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=allied&topic=banking&count=15)· [BOP](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=bop&topic=banking&count=15)
## Put It All Together 
Topic quizzes build section-wise strength, but the real test mixes everything under a time limit. When you are scoring consistently above 60% in each topic, move to a [full-length test](https://banktesthelp.github.io/mock.html)— and follow our [4–6 week study plan](https://banktesthelp.github.io/preparation-guide.html)to structure your preparation. For bank-specific strategy, read our [SBOTS 29th Batch guide](https://banktesthelp.github.io/sbots-guide.html)and [Meezan PBO guide](https://banktesthelp.github.io/meezan-pbo-guide.html)— and once you clear the written test, prepare for the next stage with our [bank interview tips](https://banktesthelp.github.io/bank-interview-tips.html).

# How to Prepare for Bank Tests in Pakistan — 4–6 Week Study Plan | BankTest.pk

Source: https://banktesthelp.github.io/preparation-guide.html
# How to Prepare for Bank Tests in Pakistan 
By BankTest.pk Team · Last updated: 26 November 2026 
Bank recruitment tests in Pakistan — whether for NBP, SBP, or commercial banks like HBL, MCB and UBL — follow a predictable format: 80 or so multiple-choice questions in 90 minutes, spread across English, mathematics, reasoning, general knowledge, current affairs and banking. The good news is that this format rewards structured preparation far more than raw talent. With four to six weeks of focused study, most graduates can raise their score from failing to comfortably above the typical 60% passing mark. This guide lays out exactly how. 
## Weeks 1–2: Build the Foundations 
The first two weeks are for learning, not speed. Start by diagnosing yourself: take one full-length test under real conditions and record your section-wise scores. Most candidates discover two weak sections and four acceptable ones — that diagnosis shapes everything that follows. 
Then work through each section systematically. For English, revise core grammar (tenses, articles, prepositions, subject-verb agreement) and start a daily habit of ten new vocabulary words with synonyms and antonyms. For mathematics, master percentages, ratios, averages, profit and loss, and interest — these five areas produce the majority of bank-test math questions. In reasoning, learn the standard patterns for series, coding-decoding and blood relations. For general knowledge and banking, begin compiling short notes: Pakistan studies facts, SBP functions, banking terms and basic economics definitions. 
Spend about two to three hours a day, rotating sections so nothing goes stale. End each study session with a short quiz on what you just covered — retrieval practice on this site is built for exactly this purpose. 
## Weeks 3–4: Per-Section Strategy 
Now shift from learning to drilling. Each section needs its own approach. In English, practice error-spotting and sentence-correction sets; these reward grammar rules you can memorize. In mathematics, learn shortcut methods — fraction-to-percentage conversions, approximate calculations and ratio tricks — because the test gives you roughly one minute per question and long multiplication is a luxury you cannot afford. 
Reasoning questions should be attacked by pattern type: when you see a series, your brain should cycle through difference, ratio, alternate and interlocking patterns automatically. That reflex only comes from volume — solve dozens of series until the patterns feel obvious. For current affairs, read national news and economic headlines daily, focusing on the last six to twelve months. For banking and finance, memorize the key terms cold: markup, collateral, LC, deposits, the policy rate and the functions of SBP and commercial banks. This section has the narrowest syllabus on the paper, so it is the cheapest source of marks. 
By the end of week four, aim for at least 60% on every individual topic quiz. 
## Week 5: Full Tests and Time Management 
Week five belongs to full-length tests — at least four of them. Sit for 80 questions in 90 minutes with no interruptions, no phone and no pausing the clock. Time management is a skill, not a personality trait, and it is built here. 
Develop a question strategy before you open the paper. Attempt your strongest section first to build confidence, then rotate through the rest. Mark questions you are unsure about and move on — a stuck question costs two easy questions elsewhere. In the final ten minutes, review the marked ones. Most bank tests in Pakistan do not penalize wrong answers heavily, so leaving questions blank is rarely wise; when in doubt, make an educated guess after eliminating the obviously wrong options. 
After each mock, spend as long analyzing as you did writing. Log every mistake in a notebook by section and by cause: concept gap, careless error or time pressure. Your revision plan writes itself from this log. 
## Week 6: Revision and Consolidation 
The final week is not for new material. Revisit your mistake notebook daily. Re-drill your weakest section with topic quizzes. Take one last full test around day three or four, then taper — light revision only in the final two days. Cramming new topics at the end increases anxiety without adding marks. 
Also use this week to read our [test day tips](https://banktesthelp.github.io/test-day-tips.html): check your documents, plan your route to the test center and sort out sleep. Logistics failures cause more lost marks than hard questions do. 
## The Mindset That Wins 
Bank tests are designed to be finished, not perfected. Candidates who clear them share three habits: they practice under time pressure, they review their mistakes instead of hiding from them, and they stay consistent for weeks instead of intense for days. You do not need to be a genius — you need to be prepared. 
Start today with the [topic quizzes](https://banktesthelp.github.io/topics.html), take your first [full test](https://banktesthelp.github.io/mock.html)this weekend, and work the plan. The passing mark is 60% — entirely within reach.

# Test Day Tips for Bank Exams — What to Do on Exam Day | BankTest.pk

Source: https://banktesthelp.github.io/test-day-tips.html
# Test Day Tips for Bank Exams 
By BankTest.pk Team · Last updated: 26 November 2026 
You have studied for weeks. The final variable is not your knowledge — it is how you manage the day itself. Bank screening tests in Pakistan are usually 80 questions in 90 minutes, and small logistical or psychological mistakes can cost more marks than a gap in your syllabus. Here is how to make sure the day goes your way. 
## The Night Before: Documents and Sleep 
Pack everything the evening before, not the morning of. Keep your original CNIC, the printed roll-number slip or admit card, and two passport-size photographs together in one transparent folder — these are the standard requirements at Pakistani test centers, though you should always check your specific instructions. Lay out comfortable clothes, a simple wristwatch if you own one, and pens even if the paper is computer-based; backup never hurts. 
Stop studying by early evening. Cramming new material the night before increases anxiety and rarely adds marks — your preparation is already banked. Eat a normal dinner, avoid excessive caffeine, and aim for seven to eight hours of sleep. A tired brain makes careless errors on questions it could otherwise answer. 
## Morning: Reach Early, Eat Light 
Plan to arrive at the test center at least 45 minutes before reporting time. Pakistani cities are unpredictable — traffic, road closures or a wrong turn can turn a comfortable schedule into a panic. Reaching early gives you time to find your room, use the washroom, settle into your seat and calm your nerves. 
Eat a light, familiar breakfast. An empty stomach distracts; a heavy meal makes you drowsy. Carry a water bottle and a small snack if allowed. Leave your phone switched off and in your bag as instructed — most centers disqualify candidates for phones ringing in the hall, so do not take the risk. 
## Time Allocation: Own the Clock 
Eighty questions in ninety minutes means roughly one minute per question. That is the entire game. Before the test starts, decide your section order: begin with your strongest section to build momentum and bank early marks. 
Set internal checkpoints. At the 30-minute mark you should be about one-third through; at 60 minutes, two-thirds. If you fall behind, speed up by skipping — never by rushing. Rushing causes careless errors; skipping preserves your accuracy for the questions you can answer. 
Each section deserves a time budget proportional to its weight. If English and math carry 20 questions each, they deserve roughly 22 minutes each. Reasoning puzzles feel engaging but are time sinks — if a puzzle resists you for more than two minutes, mark it and move on. 
## Question Strategy: Score Every Mark You Can 
Read every question carefully before looking at the options — many wrong answers are traps for readers who skim. Eliminate obviously wrong options first; your odds improve with each elimination even when you are guessing. 
Most bank tests in Pakistan do not carry heavy negative marking, and many carry none at all. Confirm the policy from the instructions on the paper, but as a rule: never leave a question blank when there is no penalty. An educated guess on a narrowed-down question is free marks. 
Reserve the last ten minutes for review. Return to marked questions, check that you have not mis-bubbled answers on the answer sheet, and make sure no question was skipped accidentally. Mismarked answers are the most painful way to lose marks because the knowledge was there. 
## Staying Calm Under Pressure 
Nerves are normal and, in moderation, helpful — adrenaline sharpens focus. But if panic sets in, it hijacks the part of your brain that solves problems. If you feel it rising, stop for thirty seconds, close your eyes, and take five slow breaths. Thirty seconds feels expensive; a panicked ten minutes costs far more. 
Do not compare yourself with the room. Someone finishing early may be guessing; someone asking for extra sheets may be stuck. The only performance that matters is yours against the 60% passing mark. Treat the paper as a set of small, independent problems — solve the one in front of you and nothing else. 
## After the Test 
When time is called, stop writing immediately and follow the invigilators' instructions. Do not argue about a question or try to change answers after submission — it is never worth it. Go home, rest, and avoid obsessively checking answers online; it changes nothing and only feeds anxiety. 
If the result is not what you hoped, remember that bank tests happen regularly in Pakistan. Analyze what went wrong — was it knowledge, time management or nerves? — fix it with targeted practice on [topic quizzes](https://banktesthelp.github.io/topics.html)and [full tests](https://banktesthelp.github.io/mock.html), and come back stronger. Many successful bankers cleared their test on the second or third attempt.

# SBOTS 29th Batch Complete Preparation Guide | BankTest.pk

Source: https://banktesthelp.github.io/sbots-guide.html
# SBOTS 29th Batch Complete Preparation Guide 
By BankTest.pk Team · Last updated: 26 November 2026 
The State Bank Officers Training Scheme — SBOTS — is one of the most sought-after entry routes into Pakistan's central bank. Selected officers join the State Bank of Pakistan as Assistant Directors (OG-2) and build careers in banking supervision, monetary policy, foreign exchange, development finance and research. Because the scheme attracts thousands of graduates for a limited number of seats, the written test is genuinely competitive. This guide explains the test scheme, shows you where the marks sit, and gives you a week-by-week plan to prepare for the 29th batch with the free material on this site. 
## What Is SBOTS and Who Can Apply? 
SBOTS is a structured induction scheme run by the State Bank of Pakistan. Fresh graduates with at least a bachelor's or master's degree (16 years of education, typically with a minimum percentage or CGPA announced in the official advertisement) can apply. Candidates go through a screening written test, followed by group discussion and interview for those who qualify. The written test is therefore the first and biggest filter: most applicants are eliminated here, which is exactly why a serious preparation plan matters more for SBOTS than for many commercial-bank tests. 
Always confirm the eligibility criteria, test date and syllabus in the official SBOTS 29th batch advertisement, because the State Bank can adjust details from batch to batch. The preparation strategy below follows the established pattern of recent batches. 
## The Test Scheme: Subjects and Where the Marks Sit 
The SBOTS written test is an MCQ-based paper, generally divided into three broad areas. Treat the following as weightage-style guidance based on the scheme's established pattern rather than a fixed promise: 
English Composition (roughly one third of the paper). Vocabulary (synonyms and antonyms), grammar and sentence correction, reading comprehension, and sometimes a short written component at later stages. This is usually the largest single block, and it is where many otherwise strong candidates lose their place. 
Quantitative and Analytical Ability (roughly one third). Percentages, ratios, averages, profit and loss, interest, and analytical reasoning — series, seating arrangements, statement-and-conclusion logic and data-based questions. Speed matters as much as accuracy here. 
General Knowledge, Current Affairs and Pakistan Economy (roughly one third). Pakistan studies, basic economics, banking and finance terms, the functions of the State Bank, and national and international current affairs from the months before the test. 
The practical lesson: do not prepare only the section you enjoy. Because the three areas carry comparable weight, a balanced score beats a brilliant one-section performance. A candidate scoring 65% in everything will outrank a candidate scoring 95% in math and 35% in English. 
## A Six-Week Study Plan for SBOTS 
### Weeks 1–2: Cover the Syllabus Once 
Start with a diagnostic: attempt the [SBOTS practice test on our SBP page](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=sbp&topic=sbots-2026&count=60)under timed conditions and note your section-wise scores. Then spend two weeks covering theory. For English, revise grammar rules and learn fifteen vocabulary words daily. For quantitative work, master the core arithmetic topics one by one. For the knowledge section, build short notes on the State Bank's functions, Pakistan's economy basics and major current affairs. Two to three focused hours a day is enough if the hours are honest. 
### Weeks 3–4: Drill by Topic 
Now switch to topic-wise drilling. Work through the [topic quizzes](https://banktesthelp.github.io/topics.html)for the State Bank — English, math, IQ, general knowledge, current affairs and banking — and keep a notebook of every mistake with its cause: concept gap, careless slip or time pressure. Analytical questions deserve special volume in these weeks, because pattern recognition only becomes fast after you have solved many series, arrangements and logic sets. By the end of week four, you should be scoring above 60% in every individual topic, not just on average. 
### Week 5: Full Tests Under Real Conditions 
Take at least three full-length tests this week, in one sitting, with a timer and no phone. Practise your attempt order — many SBOTS candidates do English first while the mind is fresh, then quantitative, then the knowledge section, returning to marked questions at the end. After each test, spend as long reviewing as you spent writing. The review is where the marks are actually earned. 
### Week 6: Revision and Taper 
Stop learning new topics. Re-read your mistake notebook, redo the questions you once got wrong, and refresh current affairs from the last six months. Take one final full test early in the week, then reduce the load so you arrive rested. Read our [test day tips](https://banktesthelp.github.io/test-day-tips.html)and prepare your documents, route and sleep schedule. 
## How the SBOTS Quiz and Free Book on This Site Help 
Two resources on BankTest.pk are built specifically for this scheme. First, the dedicated SBOTS quiz on the [SBP page](https://banktesthelp.github.io/sbp.html)gives you a 60-question practice set in the scheme's pattern, with instant scoring and explanations — ideal for your diagnostic and for weekly progress checks. Second, our free [SBOTS Batch 29 preparation book (PDF)](https://banktesthelp.github.io/sbots-batch-29-free-preparation-book.pdf)contains 400 original solved MCQs — 100 each of English, Quantitative, Analytical and Banking/GK/Current Affairs — with answers and explanations, plus the test-pattern overview and strategy notes. Use the book for untimed learning in the early weeks and the online quizzes for timed drilling later. Both are completely free. 
## Test-Day Advice 
Reach the centre early with your roll number slip, original CNIC and stationery as instructed in the advertisement. In the hall, read the marking instructions before the paper: if negative marking applies, guess only when you can eliminate at least two options. Budget roughly a minute per question, mark and skip anything that stalls you, and protect the last ten minutes for reviewing marked questions and checking that every answer is properly filled. Stay calm if one section feels hard — the paper is the same for everyone in the room, and merit is relative. 
SBOTS rewards steady, balanced preparation over last-minute brilliance. Start with the diagnostic quiz today, follow the six-week plan, and let the free book and quizzes carry your practice. The seat is competitive — but it is absolutely winnable.

# Meezan Bank PBO Test Preparation Guide | BankTest.pk

Source: https://banktesthelp.github.io/meezan-pbo-guide.html
# Meezan Bank PBO Test Preparation Guide 
By BankTest.pk Team · Last updated: 26 November 2026 
The Personal Banking Officer (PBO) is one of Meezan Bank's most popular entry-level roles, and its written test is where most applicants are filtered out. Meezan is Pakistan's first and largest Islamic bank, so its test does everything a normal bank test does — English, math, reasoning, general knowledge — and adds one extra expectation: you should understand, at a basic level, how Islamic banking actually works. This guide explains the role, the test sections, and the Islamic banking concepts you need, in plain words. 
## What Does a Personal Banking Officer Do? 
A PBO is a front-line branch role. On a typical day, a PBO opens new accounts, helps customers with deposits, withdrawals and account services, explains the bank's products, cross-sells services such as debit cards and mobile banking, and resolves routine customer queries. The job blends cash-and-counter accuracy with sales and customer service, which is why the test checks both numerical ability and communication skills — and why the interview later focuses heavily on confidence, grooming and customer dealing. It is also a genuine career ladder: strong PBOs move up into branch operations and relationship management roles. 
## The PBO Test: Sections to Expect 
The written test is MCQ-based and drawn from the standard bank-test areas. Based on the established pattern of Meezan's recruitment tests, prepare for: 
English: grammar, sentence correction, synonyms and antonyms, and short comprehension passages. 
Mathematics / Quantitative: percentages, ratios, averages, profit and loss, and basic interest-style calculations — done quickly, without a calculator. 
IQ and Analytical Reasoning: number and letter series, analogies, coding-decoding and simple logic puzzles. 
General Knowledge and Current Affairs: Pakistan studies, basic world knowledge, and recent economic and banking news. 
Banking and Islamic Finance: general banking terms plus the Islamic banking concepts explained below. This section is smaller than the others, but it is the one that separates Meezan's test from every other bank's — and it is entirely learnable in a few days. 
Start your practice with the dedicated 60-question PBO set on our [Meezan Bank page](https://banktesthelp.github.io/meezan.html), which mirrors this mix, then use the topic quizzes there to strengthen whichever section scores lowest. 
## Islamic Banking Concepts You Must Understand 
You do not need to be a scholar — you need clear, simple concepts. Learn these well: 
### Riba (Interest) and Why It Is Prohibited 
Riba means a fixed, guaranteed increase charged on a loan purely for the use of money. Islamic finance prohibits riba because money is treated as a medium of exchange, not a commodity that can itself earn more money without any real trade or risk. In an Islamic bank, returns must come from actual business activity — buying and selling goods, leasing assets, or sharing in a venture's profit and loss. 
### Mudarabah (Profit-Sharing Partnership) 
In a Mudarabah, one party provides the capital and the other provides the work and expertise. Profit is divided between them in a ratio agreed in advance; financial loss is borne by the capital provider, while the working partner loses their effort. This is the basis of most Islamic savings accounts: the bank invests depositors' funds as the working partner and shares the earned profit with them — which is why the return on an Islamic savings account is an expected profit rate, never a guaranteed interest rate. 
### Musharakah (Joint Partnership) 
In Musharakah, two or more partners contribute capital to a joint venture and share profit in an agreed ratio, while losses are shared in proportion to each partner's capital contribution. Banks use Musharakah-based structures for business financing, where the bank genuinely becomes a partner in the customer's project instead of a lender standing outside it. 
### Murabaha (Cost-Plus Sale) 
Murabaha is not a loan at all — it is a sale. The bank buys an asset the customer needs (machinery, goods, raw material), takes ownership of it, and then sells it to the customer at a clearly disclosed price: the cost plus an agreed profit margin, payable in instalments. Because the bank owned the asset and bore its risk, even briefly, the profit is a trade profit, not interest. 
### Ijarah (Leasing) 
Ijarah is leasing: the bank buys an asset — a car, equipment, a generator — and rents it to the customer for an agreed period and rental. The bank remains the owner and carries ownership responsibilities, while the customer pays for the use of the asset. Ijarah structures sit behind most Islamic car and equipment financing products. 
### Sukuk and Takaful 
Sukuk are Shariah-compliant investment certificates backed by real assets or projects; holders earn returns generated by those assets rather than interest on a debt. Takaful is the Islamic alternative to conventional insurance, built on mutual cooperation: participants contribute to a shared pool, and claims are paid from that pool. Knowing these two definitions covers most of the terminology questions a PBO test is likely to ask. 
### Current Accounts and the Qard Principle 
An Islamic current account works on Qard — the customer's deposit is treated as a loan to the bank, repayable in full on demand, and the bank pays no return on it. That is why current accounts earn nothing while savings accounts (Mudarabah-based) share profit. This single contrast appears again and again in Islamic banking questions. 
## A Practical Four-Week Preparation Plan 
Week 1: Learn the Islamic banking concepts above until you can explain each one aloud in two sentences. Revise basic grammar and start daily vocabulary. Week 2: Cover the quantitative topics — percentages, ratios, averages, profit and loss — and begin IQ series practice. Week 3: Drill topic-wise with the quizzes on the [topics page](https://banktesthelp.github.io/topics.html), keep a mistake notebook, and read banking and economy headlines daily for current affairs. Week 4: Take full-length timed tests, including the 60-question PBO practice set, review every error, and taper in the last two days. Throughout, keep your target simple: a consistent 60% or more in every section. 
## Final Word 
The Meezan PBO test is very winnable for a graduate who prepares in balance — solid English and math, regular reasoning practice, and a genuine grip on the Islamic banking concepts. That last part is your edge: many candidates ignore it, and it is the easiest section to master completely. Begin with the PBO practice set on our [Meezan quiz page](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=meezan&topic=pbo-recent-2026&count=60), work the plan, and walk into the test knowing the one section your competitors skipped.

# English Preparation Guide for Bank Tests | BankTest.pk

Source: https://banktesthelp.github.io/english-preparation-guide.html
# English Preparation Guide for Bank Tests 
By BankTest.pk Team · Last updated: 26 November 2026 
English is the section that quietly decides most bank tests in Pakistan. It is usually the largest block on the paper, it appears in every bank's screening test, and it is the section where candidates from Urdu-medium backgrounds lose the most marks — not because their English is weak, but because they prepare it randomly. English rewards system. This guide gives you that system: what to study, in what order, and how to practise every day. 
## Know What the Section Contains 
Bank-test English is built from a small set of question types: synonyms, antonyms, sentence correction and error spotting, fill-in-the-blanks (mostly prepositions and vocabulary), idioms, and one or two reading comprehension passages. That is good news — the syllabus is finite. You are not learning "English" in general; you are learning to answer six predictable question types quickly and accurately. Every hour of preparation should map to one of them. If a study activity does not clearly serve one of these six types, it is probably not the best use of your time this month. 
## Vocabulary Strategy: Fewer Words, Learned Properly 
The biggest vocabulary mistake is downloading a list of 3,000 words and trying to memorize meanings in isolation. It does not stick, and it wastes weeks. Work instead with fifteen words a day, and learn each word four ways: its meaning, one synonym, one antonym, and one sentence of your own. A word you can use in a sentence is a word you will recognize in any question format. 
Prioritize words that recur in formal and banking contexts — words like substantial, decline, facilitate, ensure, comply, estimate, vulnerable and transparent — and learn them in families: when you learn increase , also learn rise, surge, escalate and their opposites. Keep a small notebook or a notes app, and revise the whole list every Sunday. Spaced revision, not first-time learning, is what moves words into long-term memory. Test yourself regularly with the vocabulary-heavy English sets on our [topics page](https://banktesthelp.github.io/topics.html). 
## Grammar Areas That Carry the Marks 
### Tenses 
Most error-spotting questions are tense questions in disguise. Master the twelve tenses through their signal words: since and for point to perfect continuous forms, yesterday and ago to simple past, by the time to future or past perfect. Learn to spot the time marker first, then choose the tense — this single habit resolves a large share of sentence-correction items. 
### Subject–Verb Agreement 
Learn the traps: collective nouns, phrases beginning with along with or as well as (the verb follows the first subject), each, every, either and neither (singular), and uncountable nouns like information, advice and furniture (always singular, never with an s ). These few rules cover most agreement questions asked in bank tests. 
### Prepositions 
Prepositions cannot be reasoned out — they must be absorbed as fixed pairs: interested in, responsible for, good at, afraid of, depend on, consist of, suffer from, married to . Build a personal list of fifty such pairs from the questions you practise, and read it aloud daily. In fill-in-the-blank questions, choose the preposition that forms a natural pair with the word beside it rather than translating from Urdu, which is where most errors begin. 
### Articles 
Three rules handle most article questions: use a/an for a first, general mention (with an before vowel sounds — an hour, an honest officer ); use the for specific, already-known or unique things ( the State Bank, the sun ); and use no article for general plural ideas ( Banks play a vital role — not the banks when speaking generally). Practise spotting which of the three situations a sentence presents. 
## Reading Comprehension: Read the Questions First 
Comprehension passages frighten candidates because they look long, but they are the most mechanical part of the paper. Use this approach: read the questions first, then skim the passage once with those questions in mind, then read properly and answer. Most questions are answered by locating a specific line, not by understanding the whole text deeply. Never answer from your own general knowledge — the passage is the only authority, and options often include true-in-real-life statements that the passage does not say. Reserve comprehension for a fixed time budget; it should never eat the minutes your grammar questions needed. 
## Synonyms and Antonyms: The Elimination Method 
When you do not know a word, do not guess blindly. First, decide whether the word feels positive or negative in tone — this often eliminates two options immediately. Second, look at prefixes and roots: bene- suggests good (benefit, benevolent), mal- suggests bad (malfunction, malicious), -phobia means fear, -cide means killing. Third, for antonyms, beware the trap option that is actually a synonym — test setters place it there deliberately. This method converts hopeless guesses into fifty-fifty or better chances. 
## A Simple Daily Routine 
15 minutes: learn fifteen new words the four-way method described above. 
20 minutes: one grammar topic — revise the rule, then solve ten questions on it. 
15 minutes: one comprehension passage under a timer. 
10 minutes: revise yesterday's words and your preposition pairs. 
Weekly: one full English quiz and a review of every mistake, logged by type. 
An hour a day, done consistently for a month, transforms this section. Begin today: take an [English practice quiz](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=nbp&topic=english&count=15)to set your baseline, follow the routine, and re-test each week. When your timed score holds above 60% across several attempts, English stops being your risk and becomes your margin — and for the full picture, pair this guide with our overall [4–6 week bank test study plan](https://banktesthelp.github.io/preparation-guide.html).
