# Quantitative & Math Preparation Guide for Bank Tests | BankTest.pk

Source: https://banktesthelp.github.io/math-preparation-guide.html
# Quantitative & Math Preparation Guide for Bank Tests 
By BankTest.pk Team · Last updated: 26 November 2026 
The math section of a bank test is not advanced mathematics — it is school-level arithmetic performed under pressure, without a calculator, at roughly one minute per question. That makes it the most trainable section on the paper: the question types are few, the formulas are short, and speed comes from method rather than talent. This guide covers the six areas that produce most bank-test math questions, each with a fully worked example created for this guide. Learn the method in each example, then drill it on the [topic quizzes](https://banktesthelp.github.io/topics.html)until it becomes automatic. 
## 1. Percentages: The Foundation of Everything Else 
Nearly every other topic — profit and loss, interest, discounts, data interpretation — is percentages in disguise. Two skills matter: finding a percentage of a quantity, and finding the percentage change between two values. Memorize the common fraction equivalents (50% = 1/2, 25% = 1/4, 20% = 1/5, 12.5% = 1/8, 10% = 1/10) and most calculations become mental. 
Worked example: A branch's deposits rise from Rs 45,000 thousand to Rs 51,750 thousand in a year. What is the percentage increase? Increase = 51,750 − 45,000 = 6,750. Percentage increase = 6,750 ÷ 45,000 × 100 = 15% . Always divide by the original value, not the new one — that is the trap in the options. 
Worked example: A cashier counts Rs 240,000, of which 12.5% is in Rs 100 notes. How many Rs 100 notes are there? 12.5% = 1/8, so 1/8 × 240,000 = Rs 30,000. Number of notes = 30,000 ÷ 100 = 300 notes . 
## 2. Ratios and Proportion 
Ratio questions almost always reduce to one move: add the parts, divide the total by that sum to find one part, then multiply back. Keep the order of the ratio matched to the order of the names in the question. 
Worked example: A bonus of Rs 84,000 is divided between two officers in the ratio 5 : 7. How much does each receive? Total parts = 5 + 7 = 12. One part = 84,000 ÷ 12 = Rs 7,000. First officer: 5 × 7,000 = Rs 35,000 . Second officer: 7 × 7,000 = Rs 49,000 . Check: 35,000 + 49,000 = 84,000 ✓. 
## 3. Averages 
Average = total ÷ count. The test's favourite twist is the reverse question: given the average and all values but one, find the missing value by rebuilding the total. 
Worked example: A branch records deposits (in thousands) of 120, 150, 90, 180 and 160 on five working days. What is the daily average? Total = 120 + 150 + 90 + 180 + 160 = 700. Average = 700 ÷ 5 = 140 thousand . Twist: if the six-day average must be 150, the sixth day needs a total of 6 × 150 = 900, so day six must bring 900 − 700 = 200 thousand . 
## 4. Profit and Loss 
Profit and loss percentages are always calculated on the cost price , never on the selling price. Learn the two formulas: Profit % = (Profit ÷ Cost Price) × 100, and Selling Price = Cost Price × (1 + Profit%/100) for a profit, or × (1 − Loss%/100) for a loss. 
Worked example: A shopkeeper buys an item for Rs 800 and sells it for Rs 920. Find the profit percentage. Profit = 920 − 800 = Rs 120. Profit % = 120 ÷ 800 × 100 = 15% . 
Worked example: An item costing Rs 2,500 is sold at a loss of 15%. What is the selling price? Selling price = 2,500 × (1 − 0.15) = 2,500 × 0.85 = Rs 2,125 . 
## 5. Interest: Simple and Compound 
Simple interest is one formula: SI = (Principal × Rate × Time) ÷ 100. Compound interest is the same idea applied year by year — each year, interest is calculated on the grown amount. For two years, simply multiply by (1 + rate) twice. 
Worked example (simple): Find the simple interest on Rs 200,000 at 9% per annum for 3 years. SI = (200,000 × 9 × 3) ÷ 100 = Rs 54,000 . 
Worked example (compound): Find the compound interest on Rs 100,000 at 10% per annum for 2 years. After year 1: 100,000 × 1.10 = Rs 110,000. After year 2: 110,000 × 1.10 = Rs 121,000. Interest = 121,000 − 100,000 = Rs 21,000 . Notice it exceeds the simple interest (Rs 20,000) by Rs 1,000 — that difference is the interest earned on the first year's interest, a favourite test question in itself. 
## 6. Time and Work 
The whole topic rests on one idea: if a person finishes a job in n days, their daily work is 1/ n of the job. Add the daily rates to combine workers, then invert to get the days. 
Worked example: Officer A can process a file batch in 12 days and Officer B in 15 days. Working together, how long will they take? A's daily work = 1/12, B's = 1/15. Together: 1/12 + 1/15 = 5/60 + 4/60 = 9/60 = 3/20 of the job per day. Time = 1 ÷ (3/20) = 20/3 ≈ 6.7 days . Shortcut for two workers: time = (12 × 15) ÷ (12 + 15) = 180 ÷ 27 = 6.7 days — same answer, faster. 
## How to Practise for Speed 
Knowledge is only half of this section; the other half is pace. Practise in timed blocks of fifteen questions and aim to finish with a minute to spare. Do rough work neatly in columns so you can re-check quickly. When a calculation turns ugly, estimate and eliminate options — bank-test options are usually spaced widely enough for estimation to work. And never let one question consume three minutes: mark it, move on, and return if time remains. 
Work through these six areas in order, one per day, redoing each worked example with the numbers changed until the method feels boring. Then take a timed [math practice quiz](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=nbp&topic=math&count=15), log every error by topic, and drill the weakest area again. Within a few weeks, the section that scared you becomes the section you finish first — and when you are ready to mix it with the other sections under real conditions, move on to a [full-length test](https://banktesthelp.github.io/mock.html).

# Bank Job Interview Tips (Pakistan) | BankTest.pk

Source: https://banktesthelp.github.io/bank-interview-tips.html
# Bank Job Interview Tips (Pakistan) 
By BankTest.pk Team · Last updated: 26 November 2026 
Clearing the written test gets your name on the shortlist — the interview decides whether you get the job. Bank interview panels in Pakistan are not trying to trap you; they are checking three things: whether you can communicate clearly, whether you understand basic banking, and whether you look and behave like someone they can put in front of customers. The good news is that all three can be prepared. This guide covers what panels actually ask, how to build your answers, and the details candidates most often get wrong. 
## What Bank Interview Panels Usually Ask 
Most interviews follow a predictable arc. Expect questions from these five areas: 
About you: "Tell us about yourself." "Walk us through your education." "Why did you choose your degree subject?" 
Why banking, why this bank: "Why do you want to join banking?" "Why this bank and not another?" "What do you know about our bank?" 
Banking knowledge: "What does a commercial bank do?" "What is the role of the State Bank of Pakistan?" "What is the difference between a current and a savings account?" "What is markup?" For Islamic banks, expect the basics of Islamic banking as well. 
The role and customers: "What does an officer at a branch actually do all day?" "How would you handle an angry customer?" "Can you sell? How would you convince a customer to open an account?" 
Practical matters: "Are you willing to be posted anywhere in Pakistan?" "Can you work late during closing days?" "Where do you see yourself in five years?" 
None of these require genius answers. They require prepared, honest, structured answers — which is exactly what separates selected candidates from the rest of the shortlist. 
## How to Prepare Your Answers 
### Build a 60-Second Introduction 
"Tell us about yourself" opens almost every interview, and a rambling answer poisons the next fifteen minutes. Prepare a tight structure: your name and city, your highest qualification and institution, one line on any internship, work or skill relevant to banking, and one closing line on why you are sitting in this interview. Practise it aloud until it takes about a minute. Do not recite your entire CV — the panel has it in front of them. 
### Answer "Why This Bank?" With Facts, Not Flattery 
Before the interview, spend an hour on the bank itself: when it was founded, whether it is public or private sector or Islamic, roughly how large it is, what products it is known for, and any recent news — a new branch network, an award, a digital product. Then connect one or two of those facts to yourself: "I want to build my career in Islamic banking, and this is the largest Islamic bank in the country" is an answer. "Your bank is the best bank" is not. 
### Use Examples for Behaviour Questions 
For questions about customers, teamwork, pressure or selling, answer with a short real example: the situation, what you did, and how it ended. A small true story from a part-time job, a family business, university society work or even dealing with people in any setting beats a grand claim about your abilities. Panels believe evidence, not adjectives. 
### Prepare the Posting Question Honestly 
Nearly every bank asks whether you can be posted outside your home city, because branch banking requires it. If you genuinely cannot relocate, say so respectfully — but understand it may cost you the offer. If you can, say yes clearly and without conditions. Hesitation here is one of the most common reasons strong candidates are passed over. 
## Dress and Etiquette 
Banking is a conservative, customer-facing profession, and the panel judges whether you look the part. For men: a clean, pressed formal shirt with dress trousers and formal shoes, or a neat, plain shalwar kameez with a waistcoat where that is the local norm — tidy hair, trimmed beard or clean shave, no jeans, no sneakers, no strong fragrance. For women: modest, formal attire with a dupatta as appropriate, minimal jewellery and natural presentation. Arrive fifteen minutes early, greet the panel as you enter, sit only when invited, keep your phone completely silent and out of sight, maintain comfortable eye contact with whoever is speaking, and thank the panel when you leave. Small courtesies are noticed precisely because so many candidates skip them. 
## Documents to Carry 
Bring an organised file — scrambling for papers signals disorganisation. Carry: 
Original CNIC, plus two photocopies 
All educational documents: matric and intermediate certificates, bachelor/master degree and transcripts (originals plus copies) 
Recent passport-size photographs (keep four to six) 
An updated CV — two or three printed copies 
The interview call letter or email printout 
Experience letters or internship certificates, if any 
Domicile and PRC, where the advertisement asks for them 
## Common Mistakes That Cost Candidates the Job 
Knowing nothing about the bank. Five minutes of research would fix it, and panels always test for it. 
Memorised, robotic answers. Panels hear the same internet answers daily. Speak naturally, in your own words, even if your English is simple — clarity beats accent. 
Criticising previous employers, teachers or other banks. It signals attitude problems, fairly or not. 
Overclaiming skills. If you say you are expert in Excel or fluent in a language, expect a follow-up question that proves it. 
Vague career answers. "I will try my best" is not a five-year plan. Show a direction: grow within the bank, learn branch operations, aim for the next grade. 
Checking the phone, arriving late, or dressing casually. Each one quietly ends interviews before they begin. 
## Final Word 
An interview is a conversation with a purpose: the panel wants to leave the room confident about you. Help them. Prepare your introduction, research the bank, revise basic banking concepts from our [topics page](https://banktesthelp.github.io/topics.html), organise your documents the night before, and arrive early and composed. If you are still at the written-test stage, start with our [bank test preparation guide](https://banktesthelp.github.io/preparation-guide.html)and the practice quizzes — the interview tips on this page will be waiting for you when your name reaches the shortlist, and our [test day tips](https://banktesthelp.github.io/test-day-tips.html)cover the logistics of getting there calmly.

# SBOTS 29th Batch Test Pattern & Syllabus 2026 | BankTest.pk

Source: https://banktesthelp.github.io/sbots-test-pattern-syllabus.html
# SBOTS 29th Batch Test Pattern and Syllabus 2026 
By BankTest.pk Team · Last updated: 26 November 2026 
Before you open a single book, you should know exactly what the SBOTS written test usually looks like: which sections it contains, where the marks are concentrated, and which topics examiners return to batch after batch. This page lays out the typical SBOTS 29th batch test pattern and a subject-wise syllabus you can prepare against. One honest note before we begin: the State Bank of Pakistan announces the official scheme in its own advertisement, and details can shift slightly from batch to batch. Treat everything below as the established, typical pattern of recent SBOTS batches — not as the official paper — and always confirm the final details in the official advertisement. 
## The Typical Pattern at a Glance 
Recent SBOTS written tests have generally been a single MCQ-based paper of about 100 questions, completed in roughly two hours, divided into three broad sections of comparable weight. As a working guide, candidates usually plan around this distribution: 
English Composition — roughly one third of the paper. The largest single block in most batches, and the section where the merit list is often decided. 
Quantitative and Analytical Ability — roughly one third. Arithmetic plus reasoning, where speed and accuracy matter equally. 
General Knowledge, Current Affairs and Pakistan Economy — roughly one third. Pakistan studies, economics basics, banking awareness and recent events. 
Because the three sections carry similar weight, the pattern punishes one-sided preparation. A candidate who is brilliant at mathematics but weak in English starts the paper with a third of the marks already at risk. Our [complete SBOTS preparation guide](https://banktesthelp.github.io/sbots-guide.html)turns this pattern into a six-week study plan; this page gives you the syllabus to feed into that plan. 
## Section 1: English Composition — Syllabus 
English in SBOTS is a test of precision, not literature. The recurring topic areas are: 
Vocabulary: synonyms, antonyms and word meanings in context. Build a daily word list and revise it cumulatively. 
Grammar and sentence correction: subject–verb agreement, tenses, articles, prepositions, pronouns, active and passive voice, direct and indirect speech, and spotting the grammatically wrong part of a sentence. 
Sentence completion: choosing the word or phrase that completes a sentence correctly and logically. 
Reading comprehension: a passage followed by questions on its main idea, details, inference and vocabulary-in-context. 
Prepare with rules plus volume: learn a grammar rule, then immediately solve questions on it. Our [English preparation guide](https://banktesthelp.github.io/english-preparation-guide.html)organises this process, and the topic quizzes on the [SBP page](https://banktesthelp.github.io/sbp.html)let you drill each sub-topic separately. 
## Section 2: Quantitative and Analytical Ability — Syllabus 
The quantitative half covers school-level arithmetic applied at speed: percentages, ratios and proportions, averages, profit and loss, simple and compound interest, partnership, time and work, time and distance, basic algebra, and simple data interpretation from tables and charts. Nothing here requires advanced mathematics — it requires fast, error-free method. Learn the shortcut for each topic, but understand the full method first, because examiners vary the numbers to defeat memorised tricks. 
The analytical half tests structured thinking: number and letter series, coding and decoding, seating and ordering arrangements, statement-and-conclusion and statement-and-assumption questions, and small logic puzzles. These questions reward practice volume more than any other area; patterns become visible only after you have solved many of them. Work through the quantitative topics in our [math preparation guide](https://banktesthelp.github.io/math-preparation-guide.html)and then mix arithmetic and reasoning in timed sets. 
## Section 3: General Knowledge, Current Affairs and Economy — Syllabus 
This section connects the test to the institution you are joining. The recurring areas are Pakistan studies (history, geography, constitutional basics), the functions and structure of the State Bank of Pakistan, Pakistan economy fundamentals (budget, trade, inflation, remittances, agriculture and industry), banking and finance terminology, and current affairs from the months immediately before the test — national events, major international developments, sports and honours. Because the employer is the central bank, economic and banking awareness carries more weight here than in most commercial-bank tests, so do not treat this section as a light add-on. Our [current affairs preparation method](https://banktesthelp.github.io/current-affairs-preparation.html)shows how to cover it in twenty minutes a day. 
## How to Prepare Against This Pattern 
Start with a diagnosis: attempt the dedicated [60-question SBOTS practice set](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=sbp&topic=sbots-2026&count=60)in one timed sitting and record your score in each section separately. Then divide your study time in the same proportion as the paper — roughly a third each — with extra time on whichever section your diagnostic exposed as weakest. Drill topic by topic using the [topic quizzes](https://banktesthelp.github.io/topics.html), keep a written notebook of every mistake and its cause, and finish your preparation with full-length tests under exam conditions. The free [SBOTS Batch 29 preparation book (PDF)](https://banktesthelp.github.io/sbots-batch-29-free-preparation-book.pdf)gives you 400 original solved MCQs organised by section, which matches this pattern-based approach exactly. 
The SBOTS pattern is demanding but predictable. Candidates who prepare section by section, in proportion to the marks, consistently outperform candidates who simply study harder in one favourite subject. Know the pattern, cover the syllabus, and practise under time — that is the whole formula.

# Meezan Bank PBO Test Pattern & Syllabus | BankTest.pk

Source: https://banktesthelp.github.io/meezan-pbo-test-pattern.html
# Meezan Bank PBO Test Pattern and Syllabus 
By BankTest.pk Team · Last updated: 26 November 2026 
The Personal Banking Officer (PBO) programme is one of Meezan Bank's main entry routes for fresh graduates who want a career in branch banking and customer relationship roles. Because Meezan is Pakistan's largest Islamic bank, its recruitment test follows the familiar bank-test pattern — English, mathematics, IQ and general knowledge — with one addition that catches many candidates off guard: a genuine Islamic banking component. This page explains the typical PBO test pattern, the syllabus under each section, and how to prepare, including the Islamic banking portion. As with all bank tests, the bank's own advertisement and instructions are final; what follows is the typical pattern these tests follow. 
## The Typical PBO Test Pattern 
PBO screening tests are generally MCQ-based, computer- or paper-based depending on the hiring round, and built from five areas: 
English — comprehension, grammar and vocabulary. 
Mathematics / Quantitative — everyday arithmetic at speed. 
IQ and Reasoning — series, analogies and logic. 
General Knowledge and Current Affairs — Pakistan-focused facts and recent events. 
Islamic Banking and Banking Awareness — the section that separates Meezan's test from conventional-bank tests. 
The exact number of questions and the weight of each section can vary between hiring rounds, so prepare all five areas rather than gambling on a fixed distribution. Candidates who clear the written stage typically go on to interviews, where personality, communication and customer-handling attitude are assessed — read our [bank interview tips](https://banktesthelp.github.io/bank-interview-tips.html)when you reach that stage. 
## Section-Wise Syllabus 
### English 
Reading comprehension passages, synonyms and antonyms, sentence correction, grammar (tenses, prepositions, articles, subject–verb agreement) and sentence completion. Branch banking is a customer-facing job, so communication quality matters beyond the test as well. Use our [English preparation guide](https://banktesthelp.github.io/english-preparation-guide.html)for a structured approach. 
### Mathematics and Quantitative Ability 
Percentages, ratios, averages, profit and loss, simple interest, basic algebra, and simple word problems based on everyday banking situations — calculating charges, comparing amounts, reading small tables. Speed with accuracy is the skill being measured. The topics mirror those in our [math preparation guide](https://banktesthelp.github.io/math-preparation-guide.html). 
### IQ and Reasoning 
Number and letter series, analogies, coding–decoding, odd one out, and short logic questions. Our guide to [IQ and reasoning preparation](https://banktesthelp.github.io/iq-test-preparation.html)explains each question family with worked examples. 
### General Knowledge and Current Affairs 
Pakistan studies basics, geography, major national events, sports, and banking-sector news from recent months. A light daily routine beats last-week cramming; see the [current affairs preparation method](https://banktesthelp.github.io/current-affairs-preparation.html). 
## The Islamic Banking Portion — What to Study 
This is the section candidates most often neglect, and for Meezan it can be decisive. You are not expected to be a scholar; you are expected to understand the basic contracts and principles a PBO will meet in a branch. Focus on: 
Core principles: the prohibition of riba (interest), avoidance of excessive uncertainty (gharar), and asset-backed, trade-based financing. 
Murabaha: the bank buys an asset and sells it to the customer at a disclosed mark-up, payable in instalments. 
Musharakah: a partnership where parties share capital, profit and loss; diminishing musharakah is commonly used for home and asset finance. 
Mudarabah: one party provides capital, the other provides effort and management; profit is shared by agreement, loss of capital falls on the investor. 
Ijarah: leasing — the bank owns an asset and rents its use to the customer. 
Deposit side: how Islamic current and savings accounts are structured on Mudarabah or Qard principles instead of fixed interest. 
Our explainer on [banking and finance concepts](https://banktesthelp.github.io/banking-mcqs-concepts.html)covers each of these in simple language, and the [Meezan PBO preparation guide](https://banktesthelp.github.io/meezan-pbo-guide.html)shows how to fit them into your study plan. 
## What Happens After the Written Test 
Candidates who clear the written stage are normally called for an interview, and for PBO hiring the interview carries real weight because the job itself is people-facing. Panels typically explore why you want branch banking, how you would handle an unhappy customer at the counter, your willingness to be posted where the bank needs you, and — at Meezan — your comfort with and basic understanding of Islamic banking products. You do not need sales experience, but you do need to sound like someone a customer would trust with their account. Prepare short, honest answers, dress formally, and carry your documents in order. Those who are selected then go through medical and reference checks before training begins, so keep your academic documents and CNIC accessible from the day you apply, not from the day you are called. 
## How to Prepare for the PBO Test 
Begin with the 60-question [PBO practice set on our Meezan page](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=meezan&topic=pbo-recent-2026&count=60)to see your current level across all five areas. Then study section by section: English and math on alternate days, IQ questions daily in short sets, current affairs in a twenty-minute daily slot, and two focused sessions a week on Islamic banking concepts until the contracts feel familiar. Practise topic-wise from the [Meezan Bank page](https://banktesthelp.github.io/meezan.html)and finish with timed full tests. The candidates who do best in PBO tests are rarely the ones who know the most theory — they are the ones who prepared every section, including the one everyone else skipped.

# UBL OG-IV / BSO / RE Test Pattern & Preparation | BankTest.pk

Source: https://banktesthelp.github.io/ubl-test-pattern.html
# UBL OG-IV / BSO / RE Test Pattern and Preparation 
By BankTest.pk Team · Last updated: 26 November 2026 
United Bank Limited hires fresh and early-career talent into several entry-level roles, and three titles appear again and again in its advertisements: Officer Grade-IV (OG-IV), Branch Services Officer (BSO) and Retail Executive (RE). Each role has its own flavour — OG-IV is a general officer track, the BSO focuses on branch operations and services, and the RE is a sales-and-relationship role for retail banking products — but their written screening tests are built from the same familiar bank-test ingredients. This page explains the typical test pattern for these UBL roles, the syllabus under each section, and a practical way to prepare. The bank's official advertisement for any specific hiring round remains the final word; the pattern below is the typical structure these tests follow. 
## The Typical Test Pattern 
UBL entry-level screening tests are generally MCQ-based and timed, drawn from five areas: 
English Language — comprehension, grammar, vocabulary. 
Quantitative Ability — arithmetic and basic data handling. 
IQ and Analytical Reasoning — series, analogies, logic. 
General Knowledge and Current Affairs — Pakistan and the wider world. 
Banking and Business Awareness — basic banking terms, products and the role applied for. 
Tests for these roles are usually speed-oriented: a moderate number of questions against a tight clock, so the deciding skill is answering straightforward questions quickly and correctly rather than solving a few very hard ones. Depending on the role and round, short-listed candidates may face further assessment and interviews, where communication and customer orientation matter — especially for BSO and RE positions. 
## Section-Wise Syllabus 
### English 
Reading comprehension, synonyms and antonyms, sentence correction, common grammar (tenses, prepositions, subject–verb agreement) and sentence completion. For customer-facing roles, clear everyday English is the point. Follow the routine in our [English preparation guide](https://banktesthelp.github.io/english-preparation-guide.html)and drill from the [UBL page](https://banktesthelp.github.io/ubl.html). 
### Quantitative Ability 
Percentages, ratios and proportions, averages, profit and loss, simple interest, basic algebra, and interpretation of small tables and charts. Branch work involves figures all day — charges, targets, balances — and the test reflects that. Our [math preparation guide](https://banktesthelp.github.io/math-preparation-guide.html)covers each topic with worked examples. 
### IQ and Analytical Reasoning 
Number and letter series, coding–decoding, analogies, odd one out, blood relations and short logic sets. See the worked examples in our [IQ and reasoning preparation guide](https://banktesthelp.github.io/iq-test-preparation.html), then practise in timed sets. 
### General Knowledge, Current Affairs and Banking Awareness 
Pakistan studies basics, major current events, sports, and everyday banking: account types, cards, digital banking channels, and what branch officers actually do. Keep a light daily current-affairs habit using the [current affairs method](https://banktesthelp.github.io/current-affairs-preparation.html), and revise core terms from our [banking concepts explainer](https://banktesthelp.github.io/banking-mcqs-concepts.html). 
## Role-Specific Preparation Notes 
OG-IV applicants should prepare the full pattern evenly, since the officer track draws on every section. BSO applicants benefit from extra attention to accuracy-based work — arithmetic care, detail-spotting and banking operations basics — because the role is operations-heavy. RE applicants should expect the same written pattern but should also prepare for interview questions about sales attitude, product knowledge and dealing with customers, since the role is target-driven. In all three cases the written test is the first filter: clear it comfortably and the rest of the process opens up. 
## What Test Day Usually Looks Like 
Expect a formal, tightly run process. You will typically report well before the start time with your roll number slip or admit card and your original CNIC; latecomers are usually not accommodated, so plan your route with a generous margin. Seating is assigned, mobile phones are not permitted in the hall, and the invigilators explain the marking rules before the paper begins — listen carefully, because whether wrong answers carry a penalty decides how aggressively you should guess. Some hiring rounds are conducted on computer at designated centres and others on paper with an answer sheet; the preparation is identical either way, but if your test is computer-based, spend the first minute getting comfortable with the on-screen timer and the review or flag option, which lets you return to skipped questions at the end. Budget your time by section rather than by the whole paper: decide in advance, for example, that English gets a fixed share of the clock, and move on when that share is spent even if two questions remain. Candidates rarely fail these tests on knowledge alone — they fail by spending twelve minutes rescuing three hard questions while twenty easy ones sat unanswered behind them. 
## A Simple Preparation Routine 
Start by attempting the [recent-pattern UBL practice set](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=ubl&topic=recent-pattern-2026&count=60)in one timed sitting and note your section scores honestly. Over the following weeks, alternate English and quantitative study days, solve a short IQ set daily, and keep current affairs to a fixed twenty-minute slot. Practise topic by topic through the [topic quizzes](https://banktesthelp.github.io/topics.html), write down every mistake with its reason, and move to full-length timed tests in the final week using our [full test](https://banktesthelp.github.io/mock.html). Before the day, read the [test day tips](https://banktesthelp.github.io/test-day-tips.html)so logistics never cost you marks. UBL's tests reward candidates who are quick, accurate and prepared across the board — exactly what a few disciplined weeks of pattern-based practice will make you.

# NBP MTO & OG-II Test Pattern & Syllabus | BankTest.pk

Source: https://banktesthelp.github.io/nbp-mto-test-pattern.html
# NBP MTO and OG-II Test Pattern and Syllabus 
By BankTest.pk Team · Last updated: 26 November 2026 
The National Bank of Pakistan is the country's largest public-sector bank, and its Management Trainee Officer (MTO) programme and Officer Grade-II (OG-II) inductions are among the most applied-for openings in Pakistani banking. Thousands of graduates compete for a limited number of seats, and the written test does most of the filtering. This page explains the typical NBP MTO and OG-II test pattern, the syllabus beneath each section, and how to prepare in a structured way. As always, the official advertisement for the specific batch is the final authority — the pattern below reflects the typical structure of these tests in recent years. 
## The Typical Test Pattern 
NBP entry-level tests are generally MCQ-based and timed, assembled from five areas: 
English Language — comprehension, grammar and vocabulary, usually a substantial block. 
Quantitative Ability — arithmetic, basic algebra and data handling. 
IQ and Analytical Reasoning — series, arrangements and logical problems. 
General Knowledge and Current Affairs — Pakistan studies, world affairs and recent events. 
Banking, Finance and Pakistan Economy — banking terms, the role of the State Bank, and economic basics. 
As a rough planning guide, English and quantitative ability together usually account for about half the paper, with the remaining marks spread across reasoning, knowledge and banking awareness. The exact counts vary by batch and testing arrangement, which is why balanced preparation beats pattern-guessing. Candidates who pass the written stage are typically called for group discussion and/or interview, where communication and confidence are assessed. 
## Section-Wise Syllabus 
### English 
Reading comprehension passages, vocabulary (synonyms, antonyms, idioms in context), sentence correction, and grammar — tenses, prepositions, articles, subject–verb agreement, active/passive voice and narration. English is a career skill in a bank, not just a test section; prepare it properly with our [English preparation guide](https://banktesthelp.github.io/english-preparation-guide.html). 
### Quantitative Ability 
Percentages, ratio and proportion, averages, profit and loss, simple and compound interest, partnership, time and work, time and distance, number systems, basic algebra, and reading tables and graphs. Master the standard methods topic by topic using our [math preparation guide](https://banktesthelp.github.io/math-preparation-guide.html), then practise against the clock. 
### IQ and Analytical Reasoning 
Number and letter series, coding–decoding, analogies, blood relations, direction sense, seating arrangements and statement-based logic. These questions look unfamiliar the first time and routine the fiftieth time — volume of practice is the entire secret. Start with the worked examples in our [IQ and reasoning preparation guide](https://banktesthelp.github.io/iq-test-preparation.html). 
### General Knowledge, Current Affairs and Banking Awareness 
Pakistan's history, geography and constitutional basics; major national and international current affairs; sports and honours; and banking awareness — functions of the State Bank of Pakistan, types of accounts, basic finance terms and Pakistan economy indicators at a general level. Build the habit with the [current affairs preparation method](https://banktesthelp.github.io/current-affairs-preparation.html)and revise terms from the [banking concepts explainer](https://banktesthelp.github.io/banking-mcqs-concepts.html). 
## Negative Marking and Attempt Strategy 
One detail decides how you should attempt the paper, and it is announced in the test instructions rather than in the advertisement: whether wrong answers are penalised. Policies differ between batches and testing arrangements, so never assume. If negative marking applies — commonly a fraction of a mark deducted per wrong answer in tests that use it — random guessing becomes expensive, and the correct strategy is to guess only when you can eliminate at least two options, which turns a blind one-in-four chance into a genuine one-in-two. If there is no penalty, leaving a question blank is simply a wasted opportunity, and you should attempt everything, saving the final minutes for your best guesses on whatever remains. Either way, work in passes: answer everything you know on the first pass, mark the questions that need thought, and return to them on the second pass with the clock you have left. Keep your attempt order deliberate — many candidates do English first while the mind is fresh, then quantitative, then reasoning, then the knowledge sections, which depend least on a tired brain. Practise this exact routine in your timed sessions, including reading the instructions page for a full minute before you start the clock, so that on the real day the strategy is a habit rather than a decision. 
## How to Prepare for NBP Tests 
Take a timed diagnostic first — the topic quizzes on our [NBP page](https://banktesthelp.github.io/nbp.html)will show exactly where you stand in each section. Then study in the same proportion as the paper: heavy blocks for English and quantitative work, daily short sets for IQ, and a fixed daily slot for current affairs and banking awareness. Keep a mistake notebook; NBP tests repeat question types relentlessly, so every error you analyse is a mark recovered. In the final ten days, switch to full-length timed tests — our [full test](https://banktesthelp.github.io/mock.html)reproduces the pressure of the real sitting — and revise your notebooks instead of learning anything new. Finally, read the [test day tips](https://banktesthelp.github.io/test-day-tips.html)and prepare your documents early. The MTO and OG-II seats go to candidates who are consistently solid across all five sections, and that consistency is built in weeks, not in the last night.

# HBL Recruitment Test Pattern & Syllabus | BankTest.pk

Source: https://banktesthelp.github.io/hbl-test-pattern.html
# HBL Recruitment Test Pattern and Syllabus 
By BankTest.pk Team · Last updated: 26 November 2026 
HBL is Pakistan's largest commercial bank, and its trainee and officer inductions attract enormous applicant pools every year. Whether the opening is for a management trainee programme, a cashier or branch role, or a specialist position, the first serious filter is almost always a written screening test built on the standard bank-test pattern. This page explains the typical HBL test pattern, the syllabus under each section, and a preparation strategy that fits how these tests are actually scored. Specific advertisements can adjust details, so treat this as the typical pattern and always read the official instructions for the round you are applying to. 
## The Typical Test Pattern 
HBL screening tests are generally MCQ-based, timed, and drawn from five areas: 
English Language — comprehension, grammar and vocabulary. 
Mathematics / Quantitative Ability — arithmetic and data interpretation. 
IQ and Logical Reasoning — series, analogies and problem-solving. 
General Knowledge and Current Affairs — Pakistan and world awareness. 
Banking and Business Awareness — basic banking, accounts and customer concepts. 
Two features define these tests. First, they are speed tests in disguise: the questions are mostly moderate, but the clock is tight, so candidates who manage time well outscore candidates who merely know more. Second, the sections reward balance — a very weak performance in any one area can end an otherwise strong application. Short-listed candidates normally proceed to interviews, and for some programmes to group exercises or assessment activities. 
## Section-Wise Syllabus 
### English 
Comprehension passages with inference questions, synonyms and antonyms, sentence correction and completion, and core grammar — tenses, prepositions, subject–verb agreement, articles and voice. HBL's customer base is national and international, and the test quietly checks whether you can communicate clearly. Use our [English preparation guide](https://banktesthelp.github.io/english-preparation-guide.html)for the method and drill daily. 
### Mathematics and Quantitative Ability 
Percentages, ratios, averages, profit and loss, interest, basic algebra, averages of data sets, and interpretation of tables, bar charts and simple graphs. Banking work is numerical work; this section is its proxy. Work through the topics in our [math preparation guide](https://banktesthelp.github.io/math-preparation-guide.html)and then practise mixed sets against a timer. 
### IQ and Logical Reasoning 
Number and letter series, coding–decoding, analogies, odd one out, blood relations, direction sense and short analytical puzzles. Our [IQ and reasoning preparation guide](https://banktesthelp.github.io/iq-test-preparation.html)explains every family of question with worked examples — read it before you start drilling. 
### General Knowledge, Current Affairs and Banking Awareness 
Pakistan studies fundamentals, geography, major current events of recent months, sports, and banking basics: types of accounts and cards, digital banking, the role of the State Bank, and common finance terms. Follow the daily routine in our [current affairs preparation method](https://banktesthelp.github.io/current-affairs-preparation.html)and revise concepts from the [banking concepts page](https://banktesthelp.github.io/banking-mcqs-concepts.html). 
## Trainee Programmes and Direct Roles: What Changes? 
Not every HBL opening tests in exactly the same way, and understanding the route you are applying through sharpens your preparation. Management trainee and trainee officer programmes recruit fresh graduates in batches; their tests lean towards aptitude — English, quantitative ability and reasoning — because the bank expects to teach the banking itself during training. Direct branch and operations roles, such as cashier and branch services positions, test the same core skills but tend to place relatively more weight on numerical accuracy, attention to detail and basic banking awareness, since the work begins immediately. Specialist hiring — IT, finance, risk, audit — may add a subject-specific component or rely more heavily on interviews and credentials. The practical lesson is to read each advertisement's own description of the selection process before you finalise your study plan: if the role is trainee-level, invest your hours in aptitude speed; if it is an operations role, add banking basics and accuracy drills; if it is specialist, revise your degree subject alongside the standard pattern. In every case the first written filter still decides who gets seen, so the core five-section preparation on this page remains your foundation. If you are applying to more than one bank at the same time — as most candidates sensibly do — this same foundation serves you everywhere, with only small adjustments per bank's advertisement. 
## A Preparation Strategy That Fits HBL Tests 
Because time pressure is the real opponent, structure your preparation in three layers. First, learn the content: one topic at a time from the syllabus above, using the guides and the topic-wise quizzes on our [HBL page](https://banktesthelp.github.io/hbl.html). Second, build speed: redo the same topics in timed fifteen-question sets through the [topic quizzes](https://banktesthelp.github.io/topics.html), aiming to finish with minutes to spare. Third, simulate: take full-length tests on our [full test page](https://banktesthelp.github.io/mock.html)in single sittings, review every error in a notebook, and watch your section scores week by week. Candidates who reach the interview stage of HBL hiring are usually not the ones who crammed hardest at the end — they are the ones who treated the test as a skill, practised it steadily, and walked in already comfortable with its pattern.

# Bank Jobs in Pakistan 2026: Banks, Eligibility & How Tests Work | BankTest.pk

Source: https://banktesthelp.github.io/bank-jobs-in-pakistan.html
# Bank Jobs in Pakistan 2026: Banks, Eligibility and How the Tests Work 
By BankTest.pk Team · Last updated: 26 November 2026 
Banking remains one of the most sought-after career paths for Pakistani graduates: structured grades, clear promotion ladders, and hiring that — at least at entry level — runs largely on open advertisement and written merit. This overview explains the landscape for 2026: which banks hire, the typical eligibility candidates need, the entry routes into the industry, how recruitment tests are organised, and how to apply and prepare. It is a general guide to how bank hiring works — always rely on each bank's official advertisement for the exact criteria of any specific opening. 
## Which Banks Hire in Pakistan? 
The employers fall into a few groups. At the centre sits the State Bank of Pakistan , the regulator, which inducts officers through schemes such as SBOTS. The large public-sector and provincial banks include the National Bank of Pakistan, the Bank of Punjab, Bank of Khyber and Sindh Bank. The big private commercial banks — HBL, MCB, UBL, Meezan Bank, Allied Bank, Askari Bank, Bank Alfalah, Faysal Bank, JS Bank, Soneri Bank and others — run the largest and most frequent hiring programmes. Meezan, as the largest Islamic bank, anchors the Islamic banking sector, where a few other full-fledged Islamic banks and Islamic windows of conventional banks also hire. Between them, these institutions advertise trainee programmes, officer inductions and branch-staff positions throughout the year. 
## Typical Eligibility — General Guidance 
Requirements differ by bank and role, but the broad pattern is consistent. For officer and trainee programmes , banks typically ask for sixteen years of education — a bachelor's or master's degree from an HEC-recognised institution — often with a minimum division or CGPA stated in the advertisement. For branch operations, cashier and services roles , a bachelor's degree (fourteen to sixteen years of education depending on the role) is commonly accepted. Trainee programmes usually carry an upper age limit somewhere in the mid-to-late twenties, while experienced-hire roles set their own ranges. Some roles specify disciplines — business, commerce, economics, mathematics, statistics or computer science appear often — while many trainee programmes accept all disciplines. Treat these as general guidance only; the advertisement for the opening you want is the only version that counts. 
## Entry Routes into Banking 
Management Trainee / Trainee Officer programmes: the premium route — a structured programme leading to officer grades, open mainly to fresh graduates. 
Officer grades (OG-I, OG-II, OG-III): direct officer inductions, including the State Bank's SBOTS (OG-2) and NBP's officer hiring. 
Branch roles: Personal Banking Officers (Meezan's PBO is the best-known example), Branch Services Officers, cashiers and tellers, customer services officers. 
Sales roles: retail executives and liability/asset sales officers, usually target-driven. 
Specialist roles: IT, risk, audit, treasury, trade and compliance positions for candidates with matching qualifications. 
## How Bank Recruitment Tests Work 
Most banks shortlist through a written test, conducted either by the bank itself or through a testing service — organisations such as NTS, PTS, OTS and IBP have all conducted bank tests, and several banks run their own online assessments. The typical paper is MCQ-based and covers English, quantitative ability, IQ and reasoning, general knowledge and current affairs, and banking awareness, with the mix and length varying by bank. Our pattern pages break this down bank by bank: start with the [SBOTS pattern](https://banktesthelp.github.io/sbots-test-pattern-syllabus.html), the [Meezan PBO pattern](https://banktesthelp.github.io/meezan-pbo-test-pattern.html), the [UBL pattern](https://banktesthelp.github.io/ubl-test-pattern.html), the [NBP pattern](https://banktesthelp.github.io/nbp-mto-test-pattern.html)and the [HBL pattern](https://banktesthelp.github.io/hbl-test-pattern.html). Candidates above the cut-off are called for interviews, and some programmes add group discussions or assessment centres. Final merit combines the stages as the bank's policy states. 
## What Banks Look For Beyond the Test Score 
Clearing the written test gets you into the room; it does not by itself get you the job. In interviews and group exercises, banks consistently look for clear spoken communication in Urdu and English, basic computer confidence — email, spreadsheets, data entry — a presentable, professional manner, and genuine willingness to accept postings and rotations, including outside your home city. Candidates from any academic background succeed when they can explain, simply and honestly, why they want banking and what they understand about the role. None of this requires connections or money; it requires the same preparation habit as the test itself, applied a few weeks earlier than everyone else applies it. 
## How to Apply — and How to Prepare 
Openings are announced on banks' own careers pages, in national newspapers, and on job portals; serious candidates check the careers pages of their target banks weekly and keep scanned documents — CNIC, photographs, degrees and transcripts — ready, because application windows are often short. Preparation, fortunately, does not need to wait for an advertisement: the test pattern barely changes, so the candidates who start early win. Diagnose yourself with the quizzes on our [topics page](https://banktesthelp.github.io/topics.html), study section by section with the guides, and simulate the real thing on the [full test page](https://banktesthelp.github.io/mock.html). If you are completely new to this, begin with the [beginner's preparation guide](https://banktesthelp.github.io/bank-test-preparation-beginners.html). Bank hiring in Pakistan rewards exactly one thing at entry level — merit demonstrated in a timed test — and that is a skill anyone can build with steady, structured practice.

# Bank Test Preparation for Beginners: A Step-by-Step Start | BankTest.pk

Source: https://banktesthelp.github.io/bank-test-preparation-beginners.html
# Bank Test Preparation for Beginners: Where to Start 
By BankTest.pk Team · Last updated: 26 November 2026 
Har saal hazaron graduates yehi sawal poochte hain: bank test ki tayyari kahan se shuru karein? If you have never prepared for a bank recruitment test before, the flood of books, PDFs and advice can feel overwhelming — and most beginners respond by collecting material instead of studying it. This guide cuts through the noise. It explains what a bank test actually is, gives you a step-by-step plan for your first two weeks, and lists the mistakes that quietly destroy beginners' chances. Follow it in order; each step is small on purpose. 
## Step 0: Understand What You Are Preparing For 
A bank test is a timed MCQ paper that checks five things: English, mathematics, IQ and reasoning, general knowledge and current affairs, and basic banking awareness. It is not a degree exam — nobody asks you to write essays or prove theorems. It rewards speed, accuracy and breadth. Different banks weight the sections slightly differently, which is why this site has separate pattern pages: read the one for your target bank — for example the [SBOTS pattern](https://banktesthelp.github.io/sbots-test-pattern-syllabus.html), the [Meezan PBO pattern](https://banktesthelp.github.io/meezan-pbo-test-pattern.html)or the [NBP MTO pattern](https://banktesthelp.github.io/nbp-mto-test-pattern.html)— and the overview of [bank jobs in Pakistan](https://banktesthelp.github.io/bank-jobs-in-pakistan.html)if you are still choosing where to apply. Thirty minutes spent understanding the test will save you weeks of unfocused study. 
## Step 1: Take a Diagnostic Test Before Studying Anything 
Beginners love to start with theory. Resist. Your first real step is a timed attempt at a practice set — use the quizzes on our [topics page](https://banktesthelp.github.io/topics.html)or a bank page such as the [SBP page](https://banktesthelp.github.io/sbp.html)— so you can see your actual starting level in each section. Write the five scores down. Almost every beginner discovers the same surprise: they are weaker in one "easy" section than they expected, and stronger in a "scary" one. Your study plan must be built on these real numbers, not on feelings. 
## Step 2: Repair the Basics, One Topic at a Time 
For English, the basics are grammar rules (tenses, prepositions, subject–verb agreement) and a growing vocabulary — fifteen new words a day, revised cumulatively. Our [English preparation guide](https://banktesthelp.github.io/english-preparation-guide.html)organises this properly. For mathematics, rebuild the school-level foundations: percentages, ratios, averages, profit and loss and interest, using the worked examples in our [math preparation guide](https://banktesthelp.github.io/math-preparation-guide.html). For IQ, simply learn what the question families look like from the [IQ preparation guide](https://banktesthelp.github.io/iq-test-preparation.html)— beginners lose these marks to unfamiliarity, not inability. Do not try to fix everything in one week; one or two topics per subject, done thoroughly, beats ten topics skimmed. 
## Step 3: Your First Two Weeks, Day by Day 
Days 1–2: Diagnostic test, pattern reading, and setup — a notebook for mistakes, a fixed daily study slot, and your target bank list. 
Days 3–5: English foundations (grammar rules plus daily vocabulary) and mathematics topic one: percentages and ratios. 
Days 6–8: Mathematics topic two (averages, profit and loss), plus your first IQ question families — series and analogies — in short daily sets. 
Days 9–11: English comprehension practice, mathematics topic three (interest, time and work), and a daily twenty-minute current affairs routine using the [current affairs method](https://banktesthelp.github.io/current-affairs-preparation.html). 
Days 12–14: Mixed topic quizzes every day, a review of your mistake notebook, and one full-length timed test on our [full test page](https://banktesthelp.github.io/mock.html)at the end of day fourteen. Compare section scores with your diagnostic — that difference is your first proof of progress. 
Two to three focused hours a day is enough for this plan. What matters is that the hours happen daily; bank tests are won by consistency, not by heroic weekend sessions followed by six idle days. 
## The Common Beginner Mistakes 
Studying only your favourite subject. The test pays for balance; a neglected section caps your total no matter how strong the rest is. 
Collecting material instead of practising. Ten downloaded PDFs teach less than fifty questions solved and reviewed. 
Never practising against the clock. Untimed accuracy is a different skill from timed accuracy, and only the second one is tested. 
Ignoring current affairs until the last week. It cannot be crammed; it can only be accumulated, twenty minutes a day. 
Skipping the review. Every practice set must end with: which questions went wrong, and why — concept, carelessness or time. 
## Step 4: Set Up Your Study Environment 
Before the plan can work, remove the friction that breaks it. Fix one place and one time of day for study, keep your phone in another room during that slot, and tell your family the hours are serious. Keep everything in one bag or folder: this notebook, a pen, and whatever book you are using. Beginners do not usually fail because the syllabus beat them — they fail because study only happened when motivation visited. A fixed slot turns preparation into routine, and routine is what carries you through week three, when the early excitement is gone and the test is still weeks away. 
When your first two weeks are done, step up to the complete schedule in our [4–6 week study plan](https://banktesthelp.github.io/preparation-guide.html)and keep the same daily rhythm. And when the test day approaches, read the [test day tips](https://banktesthelp.github.io/test-day-tips.html)so that nothing except the questions can surprise you. Every officer working in a bank today once stood exactly where you are standing — a beginner with a test to pass. Start today, start small, and do not stop.

# IQ & Reasoning Test Preparation with Worked Examples | BankTest.pk

Source: https://banktesthelp.github.io/iq-test-preparation.html
# IQ and Reasoning Test Preparation with Worked Examples 
By BankTest.pk Team · Last updated: 26 November 2026 
The IQ and reasoning section frightens beginners more than any other part of a bank test — and it is actually the easiest section to improve. IQ questions are not testing genius; they test whether you recognise a small set of repeating patterns quickly. Once you have seen each question family and understood its logic, the same patterns return in test after test wearing different numbers. This guide explains the main families with original worked examples. Solve each example yourself before reading the solution — that struggle is where the learning happens — then drill with the timed quizzes on our [topics page](https://banktesthelp.github.io/topics.html). 
## Family 1: Number Series 
Example 1: 3, 6, 12, 24, ? — Each term doubles the previous one: 3 × 2 = 6, 6 × 2 = 12, 12 × 2 = 24, so the next term is 24 × 2 = 48 . When a series grows fast, test multiplication and division first. 
Example 2: 5, 9, 17, 33, ? — Look at the differences: 9 − 5 = 4, 17 − 9 = 8, 33 − 17 = 16. The differences themselves double (4, 8, 16), so the next difference is 32 and the next term is 33 + 32 = 65 . If a series grows steadily but not by multiplication, write the differences underneath; if those are not constant, check whether the differences form their own pattern. Other common engines are adding consecutive numbers, squares (1, 4, 9, 16…), cubes, and alternating operations such as ×2 − 1. 
## Family 2: Letter Series 
Example 3: B, D, G, K, P, ? — Convert letters to positions: B = 2, D = 4, G = 7, K = 11, P = 16. The jumps are +2, +3, +4, +5, so the next jump is +6, giving 22 = V . Almost every letter series becomes a number series once you write the alphabet positions — memorise the landmarks A=1, E=5, J=10, O=15, T=20, Z=26 and count from the nearest one. 
## Family 3: Analogies 
Example 4: Book : Pages :: Wall : ? — First state the relationship in the given pair in one sentence: "A book is made of pages." Apply the same sentence to the second pair: "A wall is made of…" — Bricks . Analogy questions fail when candidates match surface similarity instead of the relationship. Always name the relationship first — part–whole, worker–tool, cause–effect, synonym, antonym, degree — and only then choose the option that fits the same relationship. 
## Family 4: Coding–Decoding 
Example 5: If CAT is coded as 24, what is the code for DOG? Test the simplest hypothesis: letter positions added together. C = 3, A = 1, T = 20, and 3 + 1 + 20 = 24. ✔ The rule works, so apply it: D = 4, O = 15, G = 7, and 4 + 15 + 7 = 26 . Other common rules are positions written directly, letters shifted forward or backward by a fixed number (A→C is +2), and reversed alphabet positions (A = 26, B = 25…). When one hypothesis fails on the given example, discard it immediately and test the next — never force it. 
## Family 5: Blood Relations 
Example 6: A man says, pointing to a girl: "She is the daughter of my mother's only son." Who is the girl to the man? Unpack from the inside out: "my mother's only son" — the mother has one son, and the speaker is a man, so that son is the speaker himself. The girl is therefore the daughter of the speaker: his daughter . The method for every blood-relation question is the same: replace each phrase with the actual person, step by step, and draw a tiny family sketch if the chain is long. Mark generations vertically and marriages horizontally, and the answer usually becomes obvious. 
## Family 6: Odd One Out 
Example 7: Apple, Mango, Banana, Potato — three are fruits; the potato is a vegetable, so Potato is the odd one out. The hidden category can be anything: fruits versus vegetables, metals versus non-metals, prime versus composite numbers, or words that share a spelling pattern. If your first category makes two items odd, it is the wrong category — look again. 
## How to Practise IQ Questions Properly 
Work in short, timed sets rather than long marathons: fifteen questions, then a full review of every mistake, is worth more than fifty questions glanced at. In the test itself, give a series question at most a minute; if no pattern appears, mark it and move on — easier marks are waiting later in the section. Keep a notebook of every pattern that beat you, organised by family; after a few weeks you will notice your notebook stops growing, which is precisely when this section turns from your weakest into your most reliable source of marks. Start now with the [IQ quiz](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=nbp&topic=iq&count=15), then try the same topic on the [SBP](https://banktesthelp.github.io/sbp.html)and [HBL](https://banktesthelp.github.io/hbl.html)pages, and finally test yourself under full-test conditions on the [full test page](https://banktesthelp.github.io/mock.html).

# Current Affairs Preparation for Bank Tests: Method & Routine | BankTest.pk

Source: https://banktesthelp.github.io/current-affairs-preparation.html
# Current Affairs Preparation for Bank Tests: A Simple Method That Works 
By BankTest.pk Team · Last updated: 26 November 2026 
Current affairs is the section candidates prepare worst — not because it is hard, but because it feels endless. There is no syllabus boundary, no single book, and every day adds more news. The secret is that bank tests do not actually reward endless knowledge. They reward steady familiarity with a defined set of areas over the months before the test, and that can be built with a small daily routine. This page gives you the method: which areas matter, how much time to spend, how to take notes you will actually revise, and how to turn news into marks. 
## Which Areas Actually Matter 
Bank-test current affairs questions cluster in predictable areas. For a Pakistan bank test, prioritise in this order: 
Pakistan's economy and banking: the federal budget's headline figures, inflation and interest-rate direction, the State Bank's major decisions, exports, imports and remittances trends, and major banking-sector news. The employer is a bank — this is home ground. Our [banking concepts explainer](https://banktesthelp.github.io/banking-mcqs-concepts.html)covers the background terms you need to understand this news. 
National affairs: federal and provincial government changes, major court decisions, national projects and agreements, and significant appointments. 
International affairs: major world events, Pakistan's relations with key countries, international organisations and their heads, and global summits. 
Sports: cricket above all — series results, tournaments, major records — plus Pakistan's achievements in other sports. 
Awards, books and honours: national civil awards, major international prizes, and notable Pakistani achievements. 
Science and general developments: major discoveries, space and technology milestones at a headline level. 
Notice what is missing: day-to-day political commentary, celebrity news and social-media controversies almost never appear. Examiners test recorded events and facts, not opinions. 
## The Monthly Routine 
Daily — twenty minutes. Read the front page and the business page of a reliable newspaper, or watch one proper news bulletin, and write down three to five one-line facts in a dedicated notebook or phone note: date, event, the names and numbers involved. That is all. Twenty honest minutes daily will cover more testable material in a month than a panicked week of cramming. 
Weekly — thirty minutes. Once a week, reread the week's notes, star the facts that feel "testable" — firsts, records, appointments, agreements, figures — and discard the noise. This weekly pass is what moves facts from "I read that somewhere" into memory. 
Monthly — one sitting. At the end of each month, condense the starred facts into a single short list and test yourself from it before looking at the answers. Facts you cannot recall get carried into next month's list. By test time, three or four of these monthly lists are your entire revision — perhaps ten pages instead of a mountain. 
## How Far Back Should You Go? 
As a working rule, tests draw most heavily on the three to six months before the exam, with major events from the past year appearing as well. If your test is near, prioritise the most recent three months first and work backwards as time allows. Also prepare the "standing facts" that are technically general knowledge but often asked alongside current affairs: heads of state institutions, capitals, currencies, and Pakistan's basic geography — our [topic quizzes](https://banktesthelp.github.io/topics.html)include a general knowledge set for exactly this. 
## Sources: What to Read and What to Skip 
Choose few sources and use them daily rather than grazing everything. One quality newspaper — its front page for national and international news and its business pages for the economy — covers most of what tests draw on, and the State Bank's own website and press releases are the most reliable source for banking and monetary developments, in the institution's own words. Monthly current-affairs digests and compiled booklets are useful in the final month for consolidation, because they organise events topic-wise, but they are a supplement to the daily habit, not a replacement for it; a digest read in the last week cannot rebuild six months of missing context. Skip forwarded WhatsApp summaries and unsourced social-media posts entirely: they mix facts with rumours, dates drift, and a single confidently wrong "fact" learned there costs exactly as much as a right one earns. If a claim matters, verify it in the newspaper or an official release before it enters your notebook. 
## Turning Notes into Marks 
Reading is only half the job; retrieval is what scores. Every week, attempt the [current affairs quiz](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=nbp&topic=current-affairs&count=15)and the topic sets on bank pages such as [SBP](https://banktesthelp.github.io/sbp.html)and [Meezan](https://banktesthelp.github.io/meezan.html), and add every missed question to your notebook as a new one-line fact. When you revise, cover the answer and recall aloud — silent rereading feels productive and is mostly an illusion. In the final week before the test, study only your monthly lists and the mistakes from your last few quizzes, exactly as our [test day tips](https://banktesthelp.github.io/test-day-tips.html)recommend for every subject. Current affairs rewards the tortoise: a small daily habit, a weekly review, a monthly consolidation. Start today and the "endless" section quietly becomes one of your most dependable sources of marks — and a core part of the pattern-based preparation in guides like the [SBOTS pattern page](https://banktesthelp.github.io/sbots-test-pattern-syllabus.html).

# Banking & Finance Concepts for Bank Tests, Explained Simply | BankTest.pk

Source: https://banktesthelp.github.io/banking-mcqs-concepts.html
# Banking and Finance Concepts Every Bank Test Candidate Must Know 
By BankTest.pk Team · Last updated: 26 November 2026 
Almost every bank recruitment test in Pakistan includes a banking awareness section, and it is the section where non-commerce graduates lose easy marks. The good news: the concepts tested are few, basic and completely learnable in plain language — examiners are checking whether you understand how a bank works, not whether you hold a finance degree. This page explains the core concepts bank tests return to again and again. Read it slowly, then test yourself with the banking quizzes linked at the end. 
## Interest: Simple and Compound 
In conventional banking, interest is the price of money: the borrower pays it, the depositor earns it. Simple interest is charged only on the original amount (the principal): Interest = Principal × Rate × Time. If Rs 10,000 is placed at 10% per year for 2 years, simple interest is 10,000 × 0.10 × 2 = Rs 2,000 . Compound interest is charged on the principal plus the interest already earned: after year one the amount is Rs 11,000, and year two's interest is 10% of 11,000 = Rs 1,100, giving a total of Rs 2,100 — Rs 100 more than simple interest. That small gap, growing over time, is "interest on interest", and it is why compounding appears in tests so often. Questions on these formulas also live in the mathematics section — see our [math preparation guide](https://banktesthelp.github.io/math-preparation-guide.html). 
## Islamic Banking: The Core Contracts 
Islamic banking prohibits riba (interest) and instead earns through trade, partnership and leasing. Five contracts cover most test questions. Murabaha: the bank buys an asset and sells it to the customer at a clearly disclosed profit, paid in instalments. Musharakah: a partnership in which parties contribute capital and share profit and loss; in diminishing musharakah , the customer gradually buys the bank's share — a common home-finance structure. Mudarabah: one side provides the money, the other provides work and management; profit is shared by a pre-agreed ratio. Ijarah: leasing — the bank owns the asset and rents its use. Sukuk: certificates representing ownership in an asset or project, the Islamic counterpart in spirit (not in structure) to bonds. These concepts matter most for Islamic banks — our [Meezan PBO pattern page](https://banktesthelp.github.io/meezan-pbo-test-pattern.html)shows how they are tested there. 
## Functions of the State Bank of Pakistan 
The State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) is the central bank, and its functions are among the most frequently tested facts in any banking section: 
Issuing currency — it has the sole right to issue banknotes in Pakistan. 
Monetary policy — it sets the policy rate to control inflation and support economic stability. 
Regulating banks — it licenses, supervises and inspects banks and financial institutions. 
Banker to the government and to banks — it manages government accounts and acts as lender of last resort. 
Managing foreign exchange and reserves — it oversees the exchange-rate framework and the country's external reserves. 
Promoting financial inclusion and development — programmes for agriculture, SMEs, housing and digital finance. 
Candidates for the State Bank itself should go deeper with our [SBOTS pattern and syllabus page](https://banktesthelp.github.io/sbots-test-pattern-syllabus.html). 
## Types of Bank Accounts 
Current accounts are for frequent transactions — businesses use them for daily payments; traditionally they earn no profit/interest because the money is fully withdrawable on demand. Savings accounts are for keeping money while earning a return, with some limits or conditions compared to current accounts. Term deposits lock money for a fixed period — one month to several years — in exchange for a higher expected return, with penalties or reduced return on early withdrawal. In Islamic banks, savings and term products are structured on Mudarabah, so the return is an expected profit rate rather than guaranteed interest. Everyday channels tested in banking sections include cheques, debit and credit cards, ATMs, mobile and internet banking, and interbank transfers such as IBFT and the national instant-payment system Raast. 
## Key Terms Worth Memoring 
Policy rate: the interest rate set by the SBP that anchors all other rates in the economy. 
KIBOR: the Karachi Interbank Offered Rate — the benchmark rate at which banks lend to each other, used to price many loans. 
Inflation: the general rise in prices that reduces purchasing power; the SBP targets it through monetary policy. 
Fiscal vs monetary policy: fiscal policy is the government's taxation and spending; monetary policy is the central bank's control of money and interest rates. 
Remittances: money sent home by overseas Pakistanis — a vital source of foreign exchange. 
Balance of payments: the record of a country's economic transactions with the rest of the world. 
## Now Practise the Concepts 
Concepts only become marks when you can recognise them inside an MCQ. Attempt the [banking quiz](https://banktesthelp.github.io/quiz.html?bank=nbp&topic=banking&count=15), then the same topic on the [Meezan page](https://banktesthelp.github.io/meezan.html)(where Islamic banking features strongly) and the [SBP page](https://banktesthelp.github.io/sbp.html)(where central-bank functions dominate). Note every term you missed, reread its explanation here, and finish with a mixed paper on the [full test page](https://banktesthelp.github.io/mock.html). A weekend spent on this one page plus the quizzes will put the banking section permanently on your side.
